reviews.author: Marshmallow
reviews.text: I had a great experience at this dental clinic. Dr. Pan is incredibly kind, patient, and very thorough in explaining every detail. I had quite a lot of questions, and he was always able to answer them clearly and provide the best possible solutions. He also took the time to explain what the final outcome of the treatment would likely look like, which really helped me feel more confident about the process.The clinic is equipped with advanced, high-tech scanning equipment, allowing the doctor to access my teeth from multiple angles and determine the most precise treatment plan.I would also like to mention the assistant, Angela, who was extremely friendly, patient, and attentive. All the other staff members were also very friendly and welcoming!The entire clinic environment is clean, modern, and well organized. reviews.author: Harry Li
reviews.text: I had my teeth whitening done at Emerald City Orthodontics Kirkland - Braces & Invisalign, and I’m really happy with the results!My shade went from 17 to 3, and honestly, my teeth have never looked this white before. The whole process started with getting impressions taken for custom trays, then I waited a bit for the trays to be ready. After that, I did two weeks of at-home whitening by wearing the trays overnight with the gel inside. I could already see a noticeable difference after just the first couple of days!At the end, I went back to the clinic for a stronger 2-hour whitening session, and the final result was seriously amazing — my teeth are SO white now.The whole team was also wonderful. Everyone was very friendly, patient, and professional, and I felt really well taken care of throughout the entire process. The office is clean, comfortable, and modern, and the facilities feel very new and reassuring, which made the whole experience even better.The only downside is that whitening can make your teeth pretty sensitive. The first couple of days, eating and drinking were uncomfortable for me, but it got better after that. After the final in-office treatment, my teeth were sensitive for the rest of the day, but by the next day it was already much better.Even with the sensitivity, I would still highly recommend it. After having yellow-ish teeth for over 30 years, it feels so good to finally see them bright and white. Totally worth it — should’ve done it sooner!

reviews.text: From the moment I walked into this orthodontic clinic, I could tell it was a really professional and high-quality place. Dr. Shi, the lead orthodontist, has an impressive background and gave me a very thorough and accurate evaluation. She put together a personalized treatment plan for me based on facial aesthetics, bite function, and long-term stability.Throughout the entire process, Dr. Shi was extremely careful and responsible. Every adjustment was done with so much precision that I always felt I was in great hands. The whole team is well-trained too—scheduling, explanations, and follow-up instructions are all organized and smooth, just what you’d expect from a top-tier clinic.Dr. Shi and Dr. Pan are also super friendly and always greet you with warm smiles. They take their time to explain everything clearly and make sure you feel comfortable. And on top of all that, the clinic has an adorable little dog “on duty,” which adds a fun and cozy vibe. Honestly, seeing the dog has become one of the highlights of my follow-up visits—it always puts me in a great mood.Now that the results are showing, my teeth look much straighter, and my overall facial balance has improved too. My smile feels more natural and confident than ever. I’m truly grateful to the whole team for giving me results that are both beautiful and healthy. If you’re looking for a high-quality orthodontic experience, I’d absolutely recommend this clinic.

reviews.text: As a physician myself, I tend to have very high expectations when it comes to medical care—and Dr. Pan and Dr. Shi have exceeded them in every way.From the first visit, they created a warm and welcoming environment that immediately put me at ease. They take the time to thoroughly evaluate each aspect of treatment and clearly explain their thinking, which I truly appreciate from a clinical standpoint.My case is relatively complex, and what impressed me most was their attentiveness and coordination of care. Dr. Pan and Dr. Shi maintained excellent communication with other specialists involved, ensuring a well-integrated and thoughtful treatment plan. That level of collaboration is not always easy to find, and it made a significant difference in my experience and outcomes.Beyond their technical expertise, they are genuinely caring and attentive, always taking the time to listen and address any concerns. I consistently felt I was in highly capable and conscientious hands.I would highly recommend Dr. Pan and Dr. Shi to anyone seeking orthodontic care—especially those with more complex needs.

Their genuine kindness and compassion have gone above and beyond what we would have ever expected!Additionally, Dr. Shi , Kevin, and Daphne have such a great bedside manner. reviews.author: Marty Greenberg
reviews.text: As an orthodontist, I’m very selective about which practices I recommend, and Emerald City Orthodontics in Kirkland, WA is absolutely one of the best.Dr. Jiayu (Fiona) Shi and Dr. Hsin Chuan (Dan) Pan have built a truly exceptional orthodontic practice that blends advanced technology, precision treatment planning, and a patient-first approach. Their credentials are top-tier, and it shows in the quality of care they deliver every day.What stands out most is how efficiently and thoughtfully the practice runs. They offer Invisalign, braces, and airway-focused orthodontics, with highly customized treatment plans and a strong emphasis on long-term results, not just quick fixes. The use of digital scanning, modern orthodontic techniques, and same-day starts makes the entire process smooth and convenient for patients and families.It’s also clear from their 400+ five-star reviews that patients consistently have an outstanding experience. You see the same themes over and over: friendly team, clear communication, efficient appointments, and beautiful results.From a professional standpoint, this is exactly what a modern orthodontic office should look like: board-certified expertise, evidence-based care, and a high-level patient experience.If you’re looking for the best orthodontist in Kirkland or the greater Seattle area for Invisalign or braces, Emerald City Orthodontics is a practice you can trust with confidence.

reviews.text: I initially visited Dr. Shi as a candidate for braces.  I had visible misalignment and suffered from a crossbite, which seems to have contributed to bruxism that I had experienced on and off for years. Since the crossbite had been deemed as practically untreatable by past providers, I simply desired cosmetic correction, preferably with a less visible and more passive treatment. We decided to proceed with the Invisalign system. At every visit she was very pleasant and professional. Dr. Shi always made me feel comfortable and made sure I was informed and involved in my treatment. Ultimately, she recommended that we try and correct some of the crossbite as well, since my teeth responded well. Not only has my smile and confidence improved significantly, my crossbite is now all but gone and the pain it caused with it! I couldn’t recommend Dr. Shi enough!

My tooth shade went from “15” two weeks ago to “1” after the treatment — the whitening effect is very noticeable! reviews.text: Cuando llegue aquí, ya había revisado otros lugares en realidad muchos antes de decidirme donde volver a utilizar brackets otra vez, yo use hace unos 10 años y no utilice los retainers como debí y mis dientes se volvieron chuecos otra vez.Al entrar vi que el centro son dueños unos chinitos y realmente pensé que me iba a decepcionar completamente ya que es lo que uno espera, sin embargo recibí una muy buena atención por parte de los doctores.No obstante ahorita estoy esperando ya que llegue  mi tratamiento de invisalign, para poder iniciar mi tratamiento.Escribo este Review porque creo que hay personas como yo, escépticas sobre la atención de personas no latinas, tengo muchos reviews en diferentes lados que me agradaron y los que no, así que este lugar es muy recomendable.

reviews.author: Jessica Caban
reviews.text: Seattle children’s orthopedic team was wonderful for our son. On a night that was busier than usual for them, we were still seen & taken care of overnight.We travelled with our son from Guatemala from him breaking his wrist, where we were told by local doctors there was no option other than surgery to place pins.After assessments at Seattle children’s, the orthopedic team were able to assure us that surgery was not necessary. The procedure was completed without surgery, and we have a happy, healthy boy in a cast home safe with us.Both of our twin boys have also spent an extended period of time at this hospital in isolation as premie babies during Covid.Seattle children’s sets our standard of care as a family. We will not be going anywhere else.Thank you for taking care of our boys time and time again.

reviews.author: Sarah C
reviews.text: We recently visited Seattle Children's for the first time because we flew our son there from our local hospital due to emergency issues that required a specialist to oversee his care—something we never imagined we would need. The care provided by the nurses, the specialist, and the gastroenterologist (I believe) — who, by the way, remarkably resembles Stanley Tucci🧐 — was outstanding. They are kind and caring, along with their entire team. Our family can't thank everyone enough, but I would definitely recommend this place. They deserve the love and support that people invest in them. The care and compassion they provide help the families who walk through their doors, trusting that they will do their best.

reviews.author: Scarlett Faltys-Burr
reviews.text: I'm connected to Seattle Children's Hospital in a few different capacities. One was in partnership with the UWMC as a researcher with Dr. Joyce Yi. Later on, I volunteered as a baby cuddler in NICU through the King County Dependency CASA Program. Lastly, my husband and I had to take our foster son to the ER department and have him hospitalized. United Healthcare tried to deny us coverage for his hospital expenses, but Seattle Children's strongly advocated for us and helped us get the coverage we were entitled to. Our foster son was a very challenging patient, but they were incredibly patient and sympathetic to his trauma history. I cannot say enough good things about Seattle Children's and will gladly continue volunteering as a baby cuddler through King County Dependency CASA Program for this wonderful hospital.

reviews.text: My son had recently had oral surgery done here , our first time and Doctor Egbert , the assistants , the anesthesiologist were AMAZING!! I’m truly thankful and blessed that we came across some wonderful people and was referred here by his dentist, they made us feel so comfortable. They kept my nerves calm by updating me during his procedure and they made him feel like he was in good hands . Thank you

reviews.author: Isabelle Peron
reviews.text: Soutien et pensées à tous nos enfants.Hôpital vraiment très professionnel, excellent, avec un service cancérologie (car t cells) à la pointe de ce qui peut se faire aujourd'hui. Des médecins, du personnel qui luttent très fort pour essayer de sauver, de guérir, de trouver de nouveaux traitements. Un relationnel très fort avec les patients et les familles. Merci infiniment de recevoir des patients étrangers. Pensées à Matéo 💕😢, Madigan 💕😢 à sa maman Mystin 💕 et à sa cousine 💕, Robin 😢,La suite n est pas pour le children's mais est très IMPORTANT.Un mot à tous les laboratoires (où qu ils soient dans le monde), ces laboratoires créateurs de médicaments novateurs, pour le cancer et d autres pathologies) ,(pour tant de malades comme Lena une jeune fille 😢 🇨🇵) ,D abord merci beaucoup pour les patients et leurs familles de chercher et de créer ces médicaments novateurs si importants.MAIS pourriez-vous vraiment accélérer l envoi de ces traitements novateurs jusqu au malade (où que ce patient soit), un envoi en extrême urgence du traitement jusqu au malade dès la demande du médicament serait très bien, (ce médicament est hélas très souvent la dernière chance du malade). Plus le délai d expédition du médicament jusqu au malade augmente, plus les chances de guérir pour le patient diminuent car pendant ce temps d attente la pathologie (cancer ici ou autre maladie)  continue à progresser 😢 et après il sera peut être  malheureusement trop tard .... 😢😢. Ces malades ont besoin de ces médicaments novateurs extrêmement rapidement.Ceci dit,Merci infiniment à tout l hôpital du Children’s, à tous ses services, pour tout ce que vous faites, pour les enfants malades et leurs familles. Votre soutien est très important.

reviews.author: chelsea hall
reviews.text: Absolute negligence tests were not performed on my son who was showing signs of purtussis even though he was vaccinated they saw the cough in person and did nothing sent him home with the same inhaler in the same antibiotics as the last time come to find out eight weeks later, he was tested at his pediatrician and he is positive. We have been to the hospital seven times for this such an oversight by a well renowned hospital. He could’ve infected so many kids at his school. He has been so severely ill to now find out. It might be too late to get him antibiotics and that he might have to have this for another hundred days. I am absolutely Irate as a parent.

reviews.author: Melissa Dingmon
reviews.text: Seattle Children’s took good care of us and our Care Team, lead by Dr. Michelle Ting and Dr. Tim Ohlsen, saved our son’s life. We will forever be grateful to the doctors, nurses, and staff.

reviews.author: Sara Taylor
reviews.text: Daughter took her daughter to ER last night. My daughter is very familiar with the facility, but had not been there in several years.Sitting in ER for 9 hours, my daughter had no access to even a coffee. The nurses were too busy to offer even water.Apparently the Starbucks that was once in the ER area is closed. ER patients or parents cannot access Starbucks in the hospital area of building unless they are admitted. That was a new policy even the ER nurses were not aware of.Management might want to consider a policy to allow ER patient family members etc access to some kind of services such as Starbucks or similar.Just sayin'.

reviews.author: Andy A
reviews.text: Took our Daughter in on Thursday night.  By Sunday they had not had her take a bath or change clothes.  Complete negligence on behalf of the caretakers there.We had to call them constantly to get any updates.  Promises to do their jobs and make it right were empty and they continued to fail us and our daughter.After a week of her being neglected by an incompetent staff and facility we decided to take her home.  We never heard from our assigned case manager.  Despite their reply that their "Family Support Team" will reach out, they won't.

reviews.author: Nicole Greene
reviews.text: We have had terrible experiences with Seattle Children's Hospital. Specifically, their gastro department. I have waited 4 months for a telehealth appointment and DAY OF they call me saying the Dr is "unavailable" and I will have to reschedule. No offer of a seeing a different provider or anything. The next available appointment? Yep, in another 4 months, if I wanted to do another telehealth, it's 5 months! This is ridiculous. I thought SCH was supposed to be the best. And this wasn't even the first negative we have had with their gastro clinic, in an in-person visit years ago the dr did not listen and would not order the tests we were requesting. Now, 7 years later, we are still dealing with the same issues and NEED answers!

reviews.author: Snarfplax Kids
reviews.text: I was going back-and-forth about posting a review about Seattle Children’s Hospital. After my son had spent almost 7 months in the hospital following a spine surgery that should’ve lasted a couple days in recovery. He had gone through Ecmo and I almost lost him numerous times. All of his pain and suffering was avoidable. My son came into the hospital with scoliosis and left with a tracheotomy. There were numerous staff members that were absolutely wonderful and supported us along the way, but there was a lot of staff members that treated us like a number that we were irrelevant. The hospital itself took no accountability for the different infections  My son acquired while his almost 7 months stay there with no compensation. There was no apology from the hospital and at the end of it my son was not able to come home. I’m devastated and heartbroken the hospital solution to everything we had gone through was for us to start talking to palliative care even though these people were wonderful. It’s completely useless. My son is 18 now and facing out of going to Seattle Children’s Hospital. Over the years of him going to Childrens we’ve had our ups and downs, but this last day was by far the worst! To summarize everything Childrens almost killed my son and I never received an apology or any thing else in regards to that. I will never forget what this hospital did to my child every day that he’s not home my heart breaks because of Childrens.

reviews.author: LaShawn Poree
reviews.text: I had an extremely frustrating experience here. I waited over 6 hours to be seen, and during that entire time, it felt like no one cared or even acknowledged what was going on. There was little to no communication about delays, and staff didn’t seem willing to help or provide updates.I understand hospitals can get busy, but basic communication and compassion go a long way especially when dealing with children and worried families. Sitting there for hours without answers or assistance is unacceptable. This experience left me feeling ignored and disappointed.

reviews.author: Kevin Paul
reviews.text: I am extremely disappointed with the care we received at Seattle Children’s Emergency Department.We brought our child in for severe ear pain that was intense enough to cause vomiting, along with a week of respiratory symptoms. Despite these clear concerns, the attending physician, Sheetal Khiyani, stated she could not see the eardrum due to ear wax. However, no attempt was made to remove the wax to properly assess the ear. We were sent home with Debrox and ibuprofen, without a diagnosis or meaningful pain relief.Within 48 hours, the condition worsened significantly, including the development of high fever and chills. We then went to Evergreen Urgent Care, where the provider was able to examine the ear and immediately diagnose a serious ear infection, starting antibiotics right away—treatment that should have been initiated during the ER visit.To add to the frustration, we are now facing a bill of over $1,500 for a visit where a basic diagnostic step was not performed. We chose Seattle Children’s expecting a high standard of pediatric care, but instead left without answers while the condition worsened.We also raised these concerns directly through feedback channels, but our experience afterward was equally disappointing. There was no acknowledgment of any shortcomings, no indication of areas for improvement, and no willingness to reconsider or adjust the bill despite the quality of care received.This experience raises serious concerns about both the quality of clinical assessment and the lack of accountability in addressing patient concerns.

reviews.author: oliver pulver
reviews.text: The mental health space has no outdoor area for kids, which it desperately needs because of the staff here do not do enough to take care of the patients! They forget half of the questions I ask them. They sit and Dilly Dally behind the desks about 7 out of every 10 hours I have unfortunately had to spend at this place. they have security come and monitor you if you tell them you need fresh air like that’s got to be a concern. they also never followed up about my x-ray for my man injury! It’s like they completely forgot about it. I just feel like a mental health unit at a hospital. Should feel like they are taking care of each patient, not just doing routine checks. This is NOT a juvie facility.

But she had given me numbing cream for my iron test I had to get a needle inside in my arm. Wasent bad but I felt like crap and felt like I has going to throw up.

reviews.author: Berthaadiliagonzales

reviews.author: Yasien B

I don’t know what i would do without seattle children’s, he was misdiagnosed 4 times before we came to seattle children’s and they diagnosed him within 3 days.

reviews.author: Carl Kinder
reviews.text: DO NOT TAKE YOUR CHILDREN HERE!!The situation with Seattle Children's Hospital is similar to the false DUI arrests by police and sherriffs in parts of the country. Officers are celebrated and promoted for exceeding arrest quotas. The result is that bad apples have been caught arresting innocent people to pad their numbers. Likewise there appears there could be some type of internal incentive at Seattle Children's Hospital that rewards specific doctors in some fasion for number of people reported to child protective services. Another theory is that disgruntled bad apple pediatricians simply report parents they don't like or take out frustrations on innocent people when they're having a bad day. You can see evidence of this in dozens of reviews here in the google reviews.An innocent family that I know, went through hell as a result of this deplorable behaviour by Seattle Children's Hospital.I had an average childhood. My parents did the best the could with the knowledge and life experience they had. I fell out of a tree one time and broke my arm doing normal childhood things. Now imagine if the doctor reported my parents to CPS and they were forced to take time away from work to defend themselves from unfounded accusations, and with absolutely no ability to stop the doctor from repeating this action to future victims. This is the very real threat that YOU face as a parent if you take your child here.You think you're doing the right thing by taking your child in for care due to a normal childhood event. Meanwhile members of the staff are carefully listening to every word you say, waiting for an opportunity to twist your words so that they can make a falsified report and forward false accusations to CPS.The family that I know who were affected by this false accusation are not just average parents. They are EXCEPTIONAL parents. Their children are happy and loved and protected. I WISH my parents had been as kind and loving and nurturing as they are to their children.Their assigned pediatrician submitted a falsified report which accused the mother of neglect and they were forced to defend themselves against false accusations. The mother entered a state of despair and depression for several weeks as a result these false allegations. They ultimately beat the false allegations after several interviews and visits by CPS which ultimately proved that the accusations were unfounded. The disturbing thing here is that this entire family suffered at the hands of Seattle Children's Hospital's actions. The only actual abuse that did occur here is the trauma inflicted on this family by the hospital - NOT the parents they falsely accused. The second disturbing fact is that this "hospital" will continue to inflict this damage and trauma onto countless other families without consequence.If anyone from the hospital staff / admin bothers to responds to this post, I'm sure they'll either give a typical fake-copy-pasted-canned-response or canned-fake-apology, or will try to justify their deplorable actions with the typical excuses they've used in other posts claiming that it's "state law for mandatory reporting by doctors if they suspect abuse", which is clearly not what's happening in some cases - it's very clear that falsified reports of abuse are being filed either for incentive or malicious reasons which is clearly an abuse of state and / or federal law and is NOT protected, so I'm premptively calling BS on these types of statements before they happen.In summary:DO NOT TAKE YOUR CHILDREN HERE!!

reviews.author: James Olin (Jimmy)
reviews.text: I don’t like Seattle, but we have to go and we have to go to Seattle the workers in the dental we’re real kind and understanding I guess I’ll give it a 10/10

reviews.author: Mark Gudaitis
reviews.text: The best!

reviews.author: Christina Short
reviews.text: They are always friendly and compassionate.

reviews.author: Yulieth Delgado
reviews.text: Excelente atención y gran eficiencia

reviews.author: M H
reviews.text: Y’all need to tell Rambo at the ocean entrance to cool out. He also goes by Mack Junior.Treating the parents like criminals and acting very aggressive towards them.This isn’t the place for his tough guy ego to be put on display.

reviews.author: Joanne Hardtke
reviews.text: We brought our child to this facility for severe, progressive abdominal pain, weight loss, dehydration, and repeated distress after eating. Our experience was extremely concerning and ultimately led us to seek care elsewhere.There was documented evidence of abnormalities in both GI notes and imaging, yet a diagnosis was placed in the chart that did not reflect the full clinical picture. Even with objective findings already in the record, it felt like that initial diagnosis continued to shape how symptoms were interpreted, despite ongoing decline and worsening condition. This was the case in patient and in the Er.We also encountered difficulty trying to address inaccurate information in the chart. Some of the documentation we believe to be incorrect was stored in the media section, and we were told it could not be directly amended, leaving information attached to our child’s record that we could not meaningfully correct.When a child has documented abnormalities, progressive weight loss, poor intake, and repeated severe pain, families depend on careful reassessment and accurate documentation. Instead, we felt that concerns were not fully reconsidered even as new clinical information emerged.We ultimately had to pursue care elsewhere in order to obtain a more thorough, multidisciplinary evaluation. I hope this feedback encourages more openness to revisiting diagnoses when objective findings are present and clearer pathways for families trying to correct inaccuracies in the medical record.

reviews.author: Roberta Tecumseh
reviews.text: I’m grateful my child is healthy and strong today. That said, our experience here was mixed.My son was transferred here after receiving excellent care at Harborview Medical Center which will always have my respect and gratitude. Unfortunately, because they didn’t have the necessary pediatric equipment, he was sent to Seattle Children’s Hospital, where he was placed on ECMO in February 2024.Some nurses and doctors were compassionate, professional, and supportive, and I truly appreciate them. However, a few ICU nurses on shifts around 2/1/24 - 2/8/24 were dismissive, rude, and lacked basic empathy toward a parent with a critically ill child.What was most concerning was the hospital social worker allowing a person who I had an active protective order against to wander the hospital when he was not permitted to be there. This was a serious safety issue and added unnecessary emotional distress during an already overwhelming time.I was exhausted, emotionally drained, and focused solely on staying strong for my son while he fought for his life. No parent in that situation should have to deal with poor attitudes or boundary violations. ICU staff should receive better training in communication, professionalism, and family-centered care especially when working with parents in crisis.I’m thankful for the good staff we encountered, which is why I gave the rating that I did, but some employees should strongly reconsider working in pediatric critical care if they cannot treat families with respect and compassion.

reviews.author: Sam Mentzer
reviews.text: SCH consistently goes above and beyond for their patients. From the doctors, nurses, down to the financial department, they are top-notch. I will forever be grateful for the best in class care I received from them!

reviews.author: John
reviews.text: Provides exceptional, family-centered pediatric care. Communication with parents is clear, compassionate, and frequent. The facility is designed to be child-friendly without being intimidating. Strong in oncology, cardiology, and behavioral health. A regional resource that inspires confidence during the most stressful times.

reviews.author: Shahed Uddin
reviews.text: Overall good experience but wait time is too long.

reviews.author: Taty Susakani

reviews.author: S Charles
reviews.text: Today, was not a good experience. Anytime we go here it's a three hour total time, waiting to see the doctor and waiting to get out.My son had to have his ears flushed because, he is known to have very very hard ear wax.The doctor specifically told us that the nurse will use warm water to flush ears out., out of trust I never bothered to check or touch the bottle to check the temperature.She began flushing and to see my son ended up saying his head was spinning, dizzy and nauseous. Honestly,  he has never had these symptoms before, I checked the temperature of the water to see it was very cold.Using cold water for flushing Ears isn't recommended so please have your medical staff trained accordingly.Fed up with the wait hours. Waiting waiting waiting...when with appointments.

reviews.author: Polina Rusak
reviews.text: Outstanding Children’s Hospital in Seattle.We had an exceptional experience at the children’s hospital in Seattle. The medical staff is truly the best incredibly professional, compassionate, and attentive. The way they treat both children and parents is simply unbelievable.Our child underwent a complex hip surgery, and from the very first consultation to the postoperative care, we felt completely supported and confident. The doctors are highly skilled and knowledgeable, and the nurses showed endless kindness, patience, and genuine care.Their professionalism combined with sincere compassion made a very difficult time much easier for our family. We are deeply grateful to everyone involved and cannot thank them enough for their dedication and outstanding care. We highly recommend this hospital to any family in need of pediatric medical care.

reviews.author: Kimani Pharrisee
reviews.text: Worst experience of my life. They will have you waiting for hours and hours while your back aches and your phone dies. With no answers. Don’t come here. Terrible place. Terrible service.

reviews.author: Mathew Holland
reviews.text: The nurses and doctors are super nice add friendly and very attentive to our child

reviews.author: Julz Ross
reviews.text: We donate cash and gifts to seattle childrens

reviews.author: Anna K
reviews.text: Horrible experience. Starting with the doctors and continuing through the nurses and CNAs, I would never recommend this place. The doctors are too busy to sit down and talk with families. Instead, they send members of the surgical team who are unable to answer specific questions.My daughter’s incisions were not healing properly. I am not a doctor, but I knew something was wrong. I raised my concerns multiple times and pushed for them to examine her more closely. Each time, I was told that this was simply how her body heals. Eventually, I refused to go home and insisted they take another look. When they finally checked more thoroughly, it resulted in emergency surgery.On top of everything, the nurses are not taught to be compassionate or understanding. Parents are going through incredibly difficult times—they are sleep-deprived, barely eating, and constantly worried about their child. Every professional nurse should know how to approach these situations, but that was not the case here. Only a few nurses showed genuine care and respect. Others rolled their eyes and talked behind our backs (RC.5)If you compare OHSU in Portland to Seattle Children’s Hospital, OHSU is far more professional and family-friendly. They take the time to connect with families and listen to their concerns and wishes. Unfortunately, our stay here felt unwelcoming and cold.

reviews.author: Jenny Zhu
reviews.text: The nurses were 5 stars but doctors assigned to us were 0 stars. Useless visit. Nothing could be diagnosed.My kid had very obvious allergy symptoms after taking the first antibiotic for his fever. It was out of business hours so we went to urgent care first. The doctor there gave us new prescription for antibiotic (thankfully, will talk later). Then they sent us to Seattle Children’s for possible Kawasaki disease.During our whole visit, we never saw the doctor. The other obviously new staff (we don’t know if he is doctor or not, but he is not the main doctor assigned to us) had no his own opinion. He kept checking with the never showed up doctor when we had questions. And the never showed up doctor insisted on keeping taking the first antibiotic even though we confirmed twice. We can’t imagine what will happen if we kept letting my kid taking that. It may cause severe medical accidents.The doctor also refused to give us the diagram he showed with us, which helped to better understand how to diagnose Kawasaki disease.We finally used the prescription from the urgent care, and my kid got better. See, we have to make our own decisions, because their diagnosis was completely misleading and wrong.Very disappointed with this visit. Especially the doctor.

reviews.author: Yonatan Ahdut
reviews.text: This was overall the best hospital experience we've had in the US.  Our 20 month old daughter broke her arm just before bedtime. The intake system at the emergency department was efficient.  All of the providers were really gentle and sweet with her.The only negative feedback would be:1) We brought our daughter in in her car seat and were forced to wake her up during intake to take her weight (as a provider myself, a ballpark weight is important for pharmaceutical purposes, but they could have asked us her weight or held on this as long as possible.2) we got in at 830pm and didn't leave until 130am.  Emergency room is not easy and getting things all aligned to get someone in and out of the door with initial presentation, radiology, orthopedic isn't easy, but this could be something that is worked on.

reviews.author: Irene njeri
reviews.text: My appointment was cancelled the morning I was  to go for my daughters appointment on a Monday and guess what??I had already taken a day off from my work place.I called again and I wanted to know why my appointment was cancelled the last day and minute and I didn't get a clear answer.i had to rescheduled again and this time I scheduled on Monday December 15th.I decided to call earlier because I didn't want to get other frustrations and guess what??we were nowhere to be seen in the calendar.I have just rescheduled again this time on Thursday next week and am not sure if I will still manage to get there.Physical therapy department you are not fair at all.

reviews.author: Lester Mejia
reviews.text: I honestly think it's the best children's hospital, but today I brought my daughter in with a very bad eczema flare-up, and they've had me waiting for four hours. They gave me a form to sign, saying it was so they could see her, but the form said I'd been seen as soon as I arrived. I understand if some people need to be seen faster, but why do this? If they don't think it's an emergency, they should tell us and not make us wait so long. That's my complaint. Otherwise, I think it's the best hospital.

reviews.author: Mikayla O'Hara
reviews.text: My son got a cut on his elbow from an aluminum lid that I had just washed, and it came off of a can of organic pumpkin. I took him to the hospital to get stitches for the wound. When the medical staff mentioned giving him a Tdap vaccine without asking for my permission, I informed them that I decline. I had done my own research on tetanus and I was confident that he wouldn't contract it, because you simply don’t in the way he had gotten cut. Despite my refusal, they insisted that it was "Standard Procedure," implying that it was not something I could decline. I stood my ground and reiterated that he would not be receiving the Tdap vaccine. Eventually, we left the hospital without the vaccine being administered. It’s been almost a year later since this visit and my kid never got tetanus.I believe that individuals should have the right to make truly informed choices about vaccines to increase our autonomy in decision-making. It seems to me that the doctor lacks proper education about tetanus and the Tdap vaccine because it appears that he administers the vaccine to anyone with a cut, regardless of whether it was necessary or not. I don’t see how the doctor can assist patients in making informed decisions with such limited knowledge about the Tdap vaccine and the fact that he never offered to show me the ingredients and the black box warning on it either.

reviews.author: Josh Ames
reviews.text: Seattle Children's needs to update their procedures or do some retraining for patient care staff to keep their egos out of patient care and do what's best for the patient.  We took our son to urgent care expecting that a place that specializes in children would have the best and most thorough care options for our child.  To appointments later, they botched his blood draw twice and made my son afraid to ever  go back to a hospital again.  We were met with a dismissive attitude by the second provider how was adamant that since he was showing signs of dehydration he must have not drank any water the day prior...as if dehydration cannot occur over multiple days.  Although we did eventually get the help my son needed and we had a cause for his medical issues, he now has a deep distrust for health care providers and blood draws.  Please check your ego at the door and recommend patients to go to the labs for blood draws where they have the expertise to get it done correctly the first time instead of forcing patients to get blood draws from inexperienced nursing staff that do more harm than good.

reviews.author: LC CV
reviews.text: I would give it 6 stars if I could. I took my child to emergencies on a Sunday and the staff was amazing and the hospital is top class. Thank you!

reviews.author: Steve Yuan
reviews.text: The whole visit experience is okay. Problem with the billing and this is a notice to the upcoming family: for urgent care visits they bill through two claims, one from hospital facility and one from medical provider. So it will come out as two copays for one single visit. Called the insurance and the hospital billing many times, their says change from "insurance should handle it" to "it has been like this for years so you should know".

reviews.author: Desiree Dutt
reviews.text: My daughter has been a Type 1 diabetes since she was 5 years old. We moved from the Midwest 8 years ago. We had the best experience there in the Midwest having consistency and personal service at a major hospital. During our time here we have been forced to go to Seattle Children’s for care, never once having a consistent provider due to turn over and/ or the provider only works particular days at a certain location. Putting the burden on families to drive all across this city to access the same provider. My child is completely self- sufficient based upon our experiences and guidance from our previous doctor. The many providers we’ve seen  have not provided any insight to her care, that we as a family cannot access through Glooko. I have paid for outside sports nutritionalist, because the ones offered have very little understanding of an athlete in relation to diabetes and management. In addition, I’m charged my co-pay plus the extra little fees (50 dollars) due to the way billing is completed at Seattle Children’s. It’s odd to have insurance and pay a co-pay but still have fees based solely on how Children’s determines to code there items. 100 dollars for a 20 minute visit (telahealth or in person) is ridiculous. Lastly, I have followed all their protocols regarding accessing forms, I have called left messages, provided emails through my chart and 13 days later- I’m still waiting for a basic letter stating my child has type 1 diabetes for my employer. I’m not sure what else to do, considering I have attached the form, called and left messages requesting this be completed. We have seen the doctor, (13 days ago) and still the department is unable to get this done. When she is 18, our family cannot wait to leave this puppy mill of a clinic. It’s absolutely painful not to have any choice in care other than Children’s. Worthless experience and treatment.

reviews.author: Tyler Pigott
reviews.text: We've been several times for urgent care.  They have been professional, kind, and keep everything clean and safe.

reviews.author: Larious Norwood
reviews.text: Thank you all for taking care of a child I love very much. I hope God continues to bless you all with your work of helping children.

reviews.author: Angelina N
reviews.text: This place and our current primary, Dr Panopoulos, are simply wonderful! We feel so blessed to live in the area and have it so easily accessible. We have a daughter who has had health issues since birth. We have consistently sought medical advice and help over 12 years. Last year, we had an incredibly scary and life threatening situation and ended up in the ER. When the nurses and team found out she was missing her middle school graduation, they set up a congratulatory poster and gifts to have our own celebration in her IC hospital room . Not only is the majority of staff professional and attentive but also so thoughtful and kind. We had another episode again in May 2025 where we again found ourselves in the ER with a life threatening situation. From the moment we checked in, we felt taken care of with Katie our ARNP, Dr Wolpert, and nurses Kayla and Britt . It was this time we met a wonderful young lady named Kate (CNA?). When my daughter lost consciousness and I found myself terrified, she was there comforting me and I felt such a sense of peace and care. We later discovered that she had her own health issues growing up, Children’s had helped her and she wanted to now give back. It was such a beautiful story and its staff like her who make such a difference. People who can truly empathize and provide support that only someone who’s been through it, can provide. The follow up care has also been wonderful from the CT scan with Radley, who was honestly the coolest and most awesome staff member we have had the pleasure of meeting, to the nurse (I can’t recall her name) who so patiently waited an hour while my daughter tried her hardest to swallow a pill camera. She was one of the most patient and understanding nurses I’ve ever come across and made what wasn’t the best situation, far better with her kindness and empathy. We even learned her daughter had the same test. Again a testament to the care and selective process Childrens puts into hiring staff. This sets them apart. I think this is their secret ingredient. Yes, they have amazingly smart and talented doctors, but they also have amazing, empathetic and thoughtful supportive staff that make it such a unique and positive experience (despite being there for scary things). We are so grateful to everyone at Children’s ❤️

reviews.author: Maye Pineda
reviews.text: Muy buena atención,todo el personal son bien amables 🥰

reviews.author: Anya Dormer
reviews.text: This hospital runs on misuse of billing codes and overcharging their patients. My daughter had a mole removed here. They charged 300$ copay, because they billed it as a "procedure" not a hospital visit. They botched the removal, and she developed a massive raised scar. We went back for a steroid injection. They charged $60 for the visit, and then a month later - they tacked another $300 to it, because apparently in this hospital a single injection is also considered a "procedure". They added this $300 to an automatic payment plan we have with them, without even the courtesy of sending us a bill. I am in the process of disputing the charges, and they could not care less, all i get from them is overdue notices. I have never seen such blatant misuse of billing codes anywhere else. Shame on you, Childrens.

reviews.author: Lim
reviews.text: For Neurology department.My son suddenly began having seizures on July 3rd of last year around 11 a.m. That day, we had to take him to the emergency room, and he was later transferred to Seattle Children’s Hospital. At around 2 p.m., he had another seizure and was diagnosed with epilepsy. I saw Dr. Miles Mcintoch and Dr. Niranjana Natarajan. He was prescribed Keppra, an anti-seizure medication, and he would need to take it for about two years.However, even after starting Keppra, our son continued to have seizures — sometimes three or four times a day. In addition to the seizures, his oxygen saturation began to drop, he struggled to eat, and he couldn’t sleep. At one point, he went two days without sleeping at all. He became extremely irritable, and symptoms we had never seen before began to appear.Even more shocking, within two months, our son lost the ability to walk. At first, he became unsteady and wobbly, then he would just sit all the time, and eventually, he was lying down all day. It felt like he was slowly dying.We wanted to see the doctor as soon as possible, but we weren’t able to get an appointment until a month later. When we finally saw the doctor and explained our son’s symptoms, the doctor asked, “Why didn’t you come in sooner?” I had been calling multiple times, and although the nurse said she would leave a note for the doctor after hearing our son's symptoms, no one ever got back to us.What was even more shocking was that the doctor didn’t seem to know the cause of the symptoms. She simply said that since he was on a low dose, we should either increase the medication or try a different one. We told her our son was already in this condition on a low dose, so how could we possibly increase it? Then she said, “If you don’t, he might die.”At that point, we decided not to continue seeing that doctor and, as parents, made the choice to stop giving our son the medication. Although he still had seizures, they weren’t prolonged. After stopping the medication, he gradually regained his strength and began to improve, though the seizures persisted for some time.I closely observed my son and also conducted additional medical tests on my own. My son had high amount of heavy metals in his body. That is why had seizure. That's because gut-brain axis. I eventually found the root cause of his seizures, and he no longer has them.I am deeply shocked that such a large and reputable hospital was unable to determine the cause of my son’s condition. I have serious doubts about the doctor’s competence.

reviews.author: Christina Gomez
reviews.text: You all took really good care of my son. That said: I am really disappointed he was given Oxycodone. He's 17 and didn't need that exposure. I've had a breast removed, and after my major surgery Ibprofrin was ENOUGH. Opioids just mask the pain and doesn't help with inflammation.  Please reconsider these dangerous drugs and their exposure to our youth.

reviews.author: James Malone

reviews.author: Lacey Stacy
reviews.text: There are not enough words to describe the man who changed shaped bettered my son’s life in a such an amazing way Dr Raymond Tse is beyond amazingly brilliant at what he does. My family my son is so blessed we were able to have his magical hands so brilliantly and diligently do his work on my boys cleft lip and palate. I remember being so scared about revisions and more surgeries and he confidently told me no he sewed my boys complete bilateral cleft for eight hours with a magnifying glass. He repaired his palate with 52 stitches. He is the man the myth the legend! We are forever grateful for you!

reviews.author: Ruhie Brar
reviews.text: I had a wonderful experience with Dr.Matthew Blessing . From the moment I walked into the office, I felt welcomed and cared for. Dr. Matthew was kind, attentive, and took the time to listen to all my concerns without rushing. reviews.author: Shane W
reviews.text: Absolutely horrible experience that included a callous indifference to patient suffering combined with a stupefying lack of professionalism.First we had to wait months to be seen. We tried everything to get in sooner because our child was suffering and unable to do basic things like go to school.  We considered medical tourism, but finally found a back door method to be seen earlier.Next, we’re seen by a PA who, after hearing the briefest of descriptions proclaimed that it was X (incurable condition) and our child would just “have to live with it.”  We asked if she’d even looked at his file.  Didn’t need to, she said.  Off you go now.  Stunned, we pushed back, demanding that she at least do her job and look at his file (which contained numerous test and lab results).  She resisted.  We pressed. Finally she pulled up his file, glanced at it for two seconds and told us there was nothing there.  Isn’t there something we can do to mitigate this?  To make it better?  Less debilitating?  She headed towards the door while suggesting dietary changes—something Google could tell you and something we’d already been doing for months without result.  We continued to advocated for our child, which seemed to really annoy her.  Finally, she gave us a prescription and left.  We were shocked!   Did that really just happen?Now our primary pediatrician is telling us we need to work through Seattle Children’s doctors moving forward.  This is truly a nightmare.  Our child needs medical help and what we received from Seattle Childrens was medical malpractice with a callous lack of human empathy.

reviews.text: I'm just a dumb Canadian who got his eyebrow split open a few blocks away and stopped by for stitches. First thing I asked was if this was the right place to go (particularly since I'm an adult) and they said definitely they'd fix me up. I come in, they grab my information, and shuffle me to a waiting area. A couple hours later I'm brought to a room and a doctor cleans out the gash and glues it up all in about 20 minutes. Not once was cost or what my insurance would cover even brought up to me. I naively thought it would be at most a few hundred. Instead I get a fun letter in the mail for $1450 (adjusted down $276). Then I go to pay online and I actually owe $1723 which I'm informed is because the bill they sent me didn't include the doctor charge and the $1726 (before adjustments) is just the room charge. Nearly 2 grand for 20 minutes of sitting in a room..I know this is probably just a symptom of a broken system, but I can't in good consciousness give this experience anything but one star. It can't be unreasonable to expect one person there along the way to bring up cost or even suggest urgent care instead. They got my money without me even knowing and next time I'm bleeding out of my face, I'll certainly be asking questions first.

reviews.text: Gender-affirming healthcare saves lives. My review will remain at one star until SCH increases transparency and support for their trans patients.

reviews.author: Jessica Klein
reviews.text: I am deeply disappointed in Seattle Children's for their decision to cancel gender-affirming surgeries for trans youth and remove all mention of these services from their website. This action is not only discriminatory but also dangerous, as gender-affirming care is life-saving healthcare backed by extensive medical research.As a social worker who works with marginalized youth, I have seen firsthand the devastating impact of denying trans individuals access to the care they need. Seattle Children's was once regarded as a leader in pediatric healthcare, but this decision sends a clear message: they are willing to abandon vulnerable patients in the face of political pressure.Washington State has strong anti-discrimination laws, and Seattle Children's should be upholding them—not caving to fear and misinformation. I urge the hospital to reinstate its gender-affirming surgical programs immediately and prioritize the health and well-being of all children, not just the ones they deem politically convenient to serve. Until then, I cannot recommend this hospital to any family seeking truly inclusive, compassionate care.

reviews.author: Gideon Shoemaker
reviews.text: I am a patient at this hospital, and I would say to try and go somewhere else, at whatever cost. I was 12 and suffering with severe chronic pain, and on the very first visit, we thought I was going to meet with my care doctor, but no, I met with a doctor's assistant. We brushed that aside and took up the plan that they put in place. I had many tests that pulled up with no results that were invasive (like a colonoscopy), which all came up with nothing. I will still bedridden from pain, and one of my assistant doctors assigned us a procedure, and we took the trek up to Seattle (driving 6 hours) to get it done. On the day of the procedure we learned that my main doctor did not want to do this procedure (on the day of) but we decided to do it anyway. They somehow "lost" or "misplaced" the results of the tests for 3 months, but after a lot of calls from us, a random doctor (who wasn't even supposed to look at it) reviewed it and saw that I had Crohn's Disease. I would give it 1 star, but the fact that they diagnosed it brings it up 1. Every few years I have routine colonoscopy's, and every time their instructions are unclear, and I have to wait for a few hours for the doctors to get ready, making my stress stomach pain worse. Most of my doctors have been good (and nurses) but just the way they do things is disappointing and annoying. You need to schedule the procedures even though they recommend them. One year, I decided to not do a colonoscopy and my parents canceled that procedure, and CPS was called on us. We cannot get referred to another hospital, and this is the best one there is for pediatric care in my immediate area. I hate to say that this is your best, and worst, option.

reviews.author: Diva Dia
reviews.text: I was so impressed with the care provided to my son for his recent surgery. Before during and “almost” after. I’ll explain…Everyone from the security to the surgeon to the nurses or even non medical staff was top notch. Our favorite outside of our surgeon of course was our night nurse Clairese she was just wonderful and quite compassionate. The therapy staff was very helpful and provided additional stretches for aftercare. The ortho staff checked on us daily including our doctor and always provided great advice in a language that both my son and I could understand. Everyone just seemed very genuine and it made me feel extremely comfortable. Upon discharge we were told there was no rush to leave as the room would be empty for the remainder of the day. Since we had already placed his lunch order prior to knowing exactly when we would be up for discharge I asked if my son wanted to stay until after it arrived. We also completed a form a couple days prior for some additional resources and were waiting for them to come in between 12 and 2 per the time listed on the application. I informed the staff we were just waiting for those two things and would head out directly after. Once everything was all done I informed my 16 yr old I was going to take our belongings to the car and pick up his meds. Our nurse Hui was sweet enough to allow me to use a cart so I could take everything at once. I informed her I was going to stop at the pharmacy on the way. I dropped off our bags and popped back up to the pharmacy. Unfortunately they had trouble locating one of his medications so I text my son so he would understand why it was taking so long. After locating the medication and receiving counsel from the pharmacist, I headed back up to our floor. As I was approaching the room I saw an older blond nurse storming out of it. I had never seen her before so I wondered why she would be going in my sons room. When she came out she immediately  walked up to the nurse station and said what is he doing in there so long to another nurse. The other nurse started saying well that’s because the mother…and stopped speaking when she saw me. I wondered if they were speaking of my son and I but acted as if I didn’t hear and quickly entered the room to see my son sitting waiting. I asked what the nurse wanted since we had never seen her before and he stated he would tell me later. After carefully getting him to the car and loading him in, he said he was ready to tell me what she said…apparently her tone was quite rude saying what are you doing in here? He said oh my mother is at the pharmacy she should be up soon. She then asks well what’s this wheelchair for? He said it’s for me I just had surgery, she then responded with well she’s been gone a really long time and just left the room. What her issue was I have no clue but she left a sour taste in my mouth after such a previously pleasant experience. I know he waited to tell me about it in the car because he knows I would have called her out on her bedside manner. I personally have been at the front desk for many years and speaking about patients and their parents all loud is for sure a no no. I wish I was able to get her name but if this is her typical personality I’m sure management will know exactly who she is when they read this. Forrest B floor 8. Please retrain whomever she was.

Children’s hospital has failed us where to go what to do now. If we do call 911 where will they take her where she is gonna get the proper care she deserves. reviews.author: S
reviews.text: ive been here multiple times for many different issues and not a single time has my experience been positive. in the ER nurses frequently forgot to bring me food, which isn't too bad. It's an ER and obviously extremely busy.staff do not respect trans people's pronouns at all here, especially in the PBMU (the inpatient psychiatric unit). they constantly misgenderd me as well as the other trans people around me (Even somone who had been there for many months)the PBMU was extremely understaffed and we were not let out of the commons room more then once the day even though we were meant to be going to group therapy, individual therapy, and much more. nurses were rude and  made inappropriate comments about peoples bodies. one very young girl (around 7) was forced to shower with the bathroom door wide open while a nurse watched her while talking to another member of staff who was male, he absolutely did not need to be there and was clearly watching the girl. not to mention this young girl was forced to shower with the door wide open while over patients were near by. doctors and nurses often spoke about private information about other patients in front of other patients but yelled (yes yelled) at us for even so much as mentioning our diagnoses or experiences. absolutely disgusting. i can not express how much the truma i have from being there. maybe one day the psychological abuse of children (or anyone!) will not be seen as a norm within psychiatry. the UN has said non-consensual psychiatric "treatment" "could well amount to psychological torture" and i could not agree more as a survivor.when i got an echocardiogram (a heart ultrasound) a student did almost the entire thing without a fully qualified doctor present. we were not told this would be happening ahead of time or asked if it was ok. i understand doctors need training but a heads up would have been greatly appreciated especially since i was half naked during the procedure. the student was very kind but the doctor would push extremely hard on me, pinch me, ignore me when i was clearly in pain, as well as touch me without any warning, she even touched me without gloves on multiple times as well as wearing her mask half way down her face! have these people never heard of cleanliness? many staff wear no mask at all even though it is hospital policywhen i had a sleep study done neither me, my family or PCP were told about the fact they had dignosied me with something and the sleep clinic is just... god so awful. the staff are rude and treat you like an idiot. they do not listen to you or even pretend they care. not to mention the fact that they will cancel your appointments with no explanation, warning, or notice. and don't expect them to keep promises, no matter how many times the nurse we worked with said she would refer us to a sleep medicine doctor, she did not. it got so bad we decided to switch to a different hospital.Doctors do not take medical emergencies seriously. i have had many catatonic episodes Infront of doctors who entirely ignored me as well as a doctor loudly shuffling cards on a cement floor while i had an SPD meltdown. i begged her to stop being so loud but she just said "im not saying anything" over and over. i have nightmares about this hospital and they have given me an extreme phobia of doctors.do not go to this hospital you will face abuse, malpractice, discrimination, and receive little to no care.absolutely awful hospital, wish i never had to go here but unfortunately for me I've got many health issues.

reviews.author: Whitney P
reviews.text: The Otolaryngology lost our pediatrician’s referral multiple times. Even after our pediatrician marked urgent on the referral they resent along with all of my son’s records, Seattle Children's still had to have their nurses talk to our pediatrician’s nurses before they could attempt to schedule an appointment. The scheduling staff would not even give me a ball park of how far out they were booked. After 3 weeks of that back and forth, I was told his first appointment would be 6 months from now. This is for an infant who has been on the strongest antibiotics available for almost 4 solid months for recurring and persistent ear infections, now has a tolerance to the antibiotics, and only needs a 10 minute surgery to get ear tubes. Really disappointed in this place.

reviews.author: Cora Padilla
reviews.text: My baby was a preemie and transferred to children’s due to health issues. I liked a few of the day shift nurses. But, there are a few nurses who are rude and unprofessional.  There were a few times the nurses looked so annoyed they had to hold my daughter, right when I walked in they were like “you can hold her if you want”. Like can I settle down first? I also knew how to grab her myself… I came to see my baby one day, and she wasn’t even wrapped in the blanket correctly. Her diaper was hanging off, her back was all wet from her pee, and she was shivering like crazy! Her hands were ice cold. The little girl my daughter was sharing room with was crying for ten minutes straight and her heart rate was spiking because of her anger. No one came for those ten minutes. I felt so bad I wanted to hold her myself! Then the nurse had the nerve to say, “omg what is going on with you.” Like what??? There are a few good nurses(mostly day shift). But, that pissed me off! Also the night shift will ask me if I have any questions. They will then say, “sorry I don’t know the answer to your question. I’ll pass it to day shift…”

reviews.author: Amber Hawkesworth
reviews.text: My son was transfered by ambulance to Children's late at night. The nurses checked us in immediately and got us settled in the emergency room. They were sweet and even brought us a big tray of snacks and food. They informed us that there were no rooms available upstairs and we would have to wait until morning. That was the only uncomfortable part. We had no blankets, pillows and we were up for more then 24 hrs with an extremely sick baby. We got admitted the next morning. That room was our home for the next 5 days. Doctors and nurses worked endlessy and gave AMAZING care to our son. In the end he was diagnosed with Kawasaki Disease. Because of the doctors and nurses my son will not have long term side effects. This hospital is amazing.

reviews.text: The people in ER are so wonderful. My daughter is 18months and had something stuck on her pupil, so you can imagine how difficult it would be to pin down a baby to get it removed. They were knowledgeable, professional and very sweet to my girl. We were there for 2 1/2 hours with the procedure alone took less than 10 min. I’m very grateful

reviews.author: Lizz Aguilar
reviews.text: Look for a better hospital if your child is going to be seen multiple times. The first time was great, but very single appointment after that was frustrating and completely unprofessional. Their excuse every time was that they were ruining behind. The first time is understandable the second time is annoying, but by the 4th time having to wait 4 hours+ each time is just ridiculous and cruel specially when you're child is not allowed to eat atleast 8 hours before their surgery. It was devastating seeing my child not eat for half the day. Dr Bauer seemed great in first appointment, but after the second one she barely made any attempts to communicate properly. When I had questions she said she would have time after the surgery only to find out she left home immediately and the nurses were unable to contact her. She was also inconsistent because she would tell me something and then tell my husband the exact opposite of what she had previously told me. We had to deal with billing issues for weeks because the hospital did not bill the insurance correctly. The worst part however was that our child "fell in the cracks" as they stated and had forgotten to reschedule her next procedure in a timely matter. If it hadn't been for us calling to see why they hadn't called in months, they would have never called. Having to see our child struggle with this condition is hard enough. It's disappointing to see a hospital be so inefficient and just add on more stress on top of everything we have to deal with. I would give 0 stars if their nurses werent so kind and attentive, but seriously save yourself the trouble and find a better hospital.

reviews.author: Chi Lee
reviews.text: We have been having frustrating and stressful experiences with Seattle Children's Hospital for last 7 months or so.My son was diagnosed with some vascular anomalies last year July while traveling to Korea after seeing three specialists there and taking a PET CT scan.  The whole diagnostic procedure in Korea took us two weeks and we brought the diagnosis and the CT scan images back home and were hoping to get the procedure done here.We got a referral to Seattle Children's Hospital's vascular anomalies department in August from my son's pediatrician here in Seattle.  It took them 6 weeks to see him with the initial doctor (director), who ended up having nothing to do with his treatment and passed him to other two doctors which took another two months or so to meet them separately.  Ultrasounds were ordered and scheduled, but when we got there to get them, we had to wait about 75 minutes when no other patient was waiting.  And then we met the other doctor a month or so later.  Then a surgery was decided and we were to wait till they schedule the surgery since it would involve two doctors.  While we were waiting for them to schedule the procedure date, one of the doctors called and said they needed to get my son's MRI now.  When we scheduled it and went there to get an MRI, they said he was not scheduled in their system.  We are just so frustrated with their poor work ethics and coordination and we don't know if it's wise to trust them and let them do surgery on my son.  We gave our comments several times but they are still having bad communication/coordination issues every time we have to deal with them. We are very frustrated and stressed.  It's our hope for their system to improve and create no frustration and stress to other families that are already under stress with their child's health issues.

reviews.author: John Portillo
reviews.text: Changed my life fr fr💪🐢

The CLS also introduced the gas mask in a fun way that was tailored to my tot’s interests.No tears were shed. We were given a phone and was updated on our tot’s surgery. We also had the case # which was listed in different areas of the hospital. We ate in the cafeteria while keeping an eye out on our tot’s case. A smooth overall experience 💯

reviews.text: Overall the hospital is good; however, some of the nurses aren’t  competent and are very rude. reviews.author: Yamaris Alaniz
reviews.text: Condition: Tetralogy of Fallot with Pulmorary Atresia.I express my gratitude for the exceptional care provided to my daughter during her recent surgery in the Cardiology unit at Seattle Children's Hospital.  The entire process, from appointments to post-surgical care, was remarkably smooth and efficient.  The friendly and helpful staff, clean environment, delicious food, excellent intensive care services, particularly Nurse Terry's professionalism, left a lasting positive impression.  Special thanks to Dr. McRae for a wonderful job and effective communication, making the experience comforting for both my daughter and our family.  This pediatric cardiology team comes highly recommended for their quality services.  Thank you!Ps. My daughter appointment was the same day of her Birthday,  the receptionist team at the Ocean building  8 floor sang happy birthday for her and did a fun dance too, she felt so special at that moment! Thank you for your kindness and compassion! You are the best!

reviews.author: Joey Martin
reviews.text: hi this will be.. an incredibly long review. but the TLDR (too long didn't read) is that seattle children's LITERALLY saved my life; that is not an exaggeration. they also helped pay for expenses that we were not able to pay due to my circumstances.on april 26th, 2022, I had a lowered immune system. I couldn't eat, had a hard time breathing, and was having intense muscle spasms daily. when i arrived at children's, they put me in an emergency care unit. and on that day, i caught the worst form of covid, my left lung collapsed, and i fell into a 9 day coma. during that duration, the seattle children's team talked to my parents and diagnosed me with an incredibly rare auto-immune disorder: Stiff Person Syndrome. after my coma, i stayed in in-patient rehab for over 3 months. they took care of me in every way, and to this day i am still treated incredibly well by the seattle children's staff.I was 17 at the time, but during my... 1000 visits i have seen a lot of children with "worse" diseases than me. the staff is incredibly kind, flexible, and understanding. I have never, EVER seen a staff member that is not incredibly caring and respectful. even to "annoying" kids who do not listen. it is an amazing place, and i couldn't recommend it enough.

reviews.author: Joseph&Kristy Berthier Jr

reviews.author: Veronika
reviews.text: We had inconsistent experience here. The team that treated our baby’s cut and put stitches in was incredible. The stitches removal was a totally different story. The first team took 20-30 minutes to remove the 3 stitches and to attempt to remove the 4th, which after the doctor’s examination turned out to be not ready for removal. They restrained our baby, who was crying as hard as we’ve never seen. After those attempts, his tiny blood vessels on the face broke and the nurses told us that was normal. Well, our baby had a traumatic experience: 3 weeks past that visit he starts crying hard when he needs to be weighed at the doctor’s visit, cannot stand the checkups and prior to that he was fine. The second visit for stitches removal was not better. The nurse did not clean the area before removal and said it was not recommended in a defensive tone. How can it not be recommended if stitches removal leads to bleeding? When we asked about it, she brought us iodine, which is not recommended to be put on open cuts. There were also no attempts to distract or comfort. I get it that employees here have to work with crying babies and some might be overwhelmed but it would be great if everyone had a good approach to these little people.
