reviews.author: Katherine Doulja
reviews.text: My recent visit to this Children's hospital was an experience that left me with a mix of emotions. I want to share my candid review based on my average experience. While there were certainly positive aspects, there were also areas that fell short of my expectations. So, here's my honest take on the hospital.First and foremost, I must commend the medical staff at children's Hospital for their dedication and care towards their young patients. The doctors and nurses treated my child with empathy and kindness. They took the time to answer our questions and provided a thorough explanation of the treatment plan. Their expertise and knowledge were reassuring, and I felt confident in their abilities to care for my child.However, I can't overlook some aspects that left me slightly disappointed. One area where the hospital could improve is its organization and efficiency. During our visit, we experienced noticeable delays in appointments, and the waiting times were longer than expected. These delays added unnecessary stress and made the overall experience more challenging for both my child and me. It would be beneficial for the hospital to streamline their scheduling and appointment processes to minimize these inconveniences for families.Another aspect that stood out to me was the lack of a truly child-friendly atmosphere. While the medical staff was caring and attentive, the physical environment felt lacking in vibrancy and playfulness. The waiting areas seemed dull and uninspiring, which could potentially make the hospital experience more daunting for young patients. I believe that incorporating brighter colors, interactive displays, and age-appropriate distractions would greatly enhance the overall atmosphere and create a more comforting environment for children.In terms of communication, I noticed room for improvement between different departments within the hospital. There were instances where information appeared to get lost in transition.

reviews.author: Lela Pola
reviews.text: Came here for our 2 month old. We came from out of town and they were able to get us in that same day for a different test that we were not previously scheduled for. I have to say from the front desk to the nurses they were amazing in explaining the procedures they performed they answered all questions and concern we had and were very gentle with our daughter they got us in quickly and eased our growing anxiety as any parent who has to take a child there. Thank you all for our 1st time experience at Seattle children's hospital.

reviews.author: Crumpdiddy
reviews.text: It took 4 hours for them to tell me why my son was admitted to the ER. And I couldn’t even see him. Mary Bridge is way better and more professional

reviews.author: Lily Kurylenko
reviews.text: I never write negative reviews. But we have been trying to make an appointment with a neurologist for half a year, and for several months we were promised the appointment would be scheduled next week because the request was still being reviewed. At the end, all we got was refusal to see us without even the reasons explained. We wasted half a year hoping an appointment would be scheduled any day.

reviews.author: Murthy Gorty
reviews.text: Such a wonderful place to take children when in need of a care.I went here first ~2010 for my eldest - the staff and facilities were so child-friendly.Now, 10+ years later, we brought our younger one and the experience is even better than the last time.Throughout the stay, it was a warm experience and we felt that our child was in the best hands possible.The staff was very competent at all layers and talk about friendliness -- we felt like we were the only patient around, judging by the time they had for our questions.We had to stay back unexpectedly over night and we were well cared for.Food was great, and was sourced in health-conscious manner and very, very in-expensive (are you listening, other restaurants?)

reviews.author: Murtadha Abdulmohsin
reviews.text: The best in the world.

reviews.author: Corrin Bash
reviews.text: Was just here with one of my children in the ER for 18 hours. After the first 15, we asked where the cafeteria was as we had been there over night and needed to eat more than vending machine garbage so we could be more present for our child. We were told only admitted patients could use the cafeteria. The bill I am about to get will be OUTRAGEOUS, as most ER bills are, and my money will some how be paying for services I was not allowed to use.

reviews.author: Jennifer Herrera
reviews.text: Update: Thank you Julie for following up the next day and for offering other appointments available this month.I had an appointment with Dr Juliana Bonilla Velez 04/10/23 at 11:20am check in time. I made this appointment 3mo ago. Just received a call 8:16am the same day of the appointment to cancel it. Seriously.. Not professional at all, this Dr and the facility does not care for the patients? I been told I need to wait until June 2023 to see the Dr?. Listen. My child has had 5 consecutive ear infections since October 2022, she is loosing her hearing literally. Does anyone know where else I can take her asap? I cannot wait 2mo. And I do not need to see a nurse practitioner no offense. I leave you with a photo of my poor 4yr old maybe this touches someone’s heart to help me get to see an ENT for my child.

reviews.author: Matt Tillman
reviews.text: Had a 4:20 Urgent care appointment. It's now 6:30 and we are still waiting. What's the point of an appointment? Very poor operations here. If they don't have staff don't schedule appointments like you're at max capacity.

reviews.author: J Vest
reviews.text: Seattle Children's is a great hospital but here's my complaint.  While filling out my son's info on mychart, there is a long list for genders to select from.  There are 2 genders...male and female.  Your list has 18 different selections for gender!  This gender stuff needs to stop.  If the child thinks they are any gender other than their God given gender, then they need mental help.  Please stop this gender madness!  Please stop confusing these kids!  I mean what is " two spirit" gender anyway?  All of this gender stuff is causing many kids to be so confused.  Then they end up depressed and suicidal and you wonder why.  We need to put a stop to this madness on our children.  Stop making this OK!

reviews.author: BAM Banter
reviews.text: The women with short black hair was absolutely horrible to me, i came to pick up my child and my child was claiming that the women with short black hair called her a spastic, i then asked the women about this and she told me to "go do one", absolutely shambolic!

reviews.author: SPRING
reviews.text: My son's pediatrician gave me a referral.  call seattle childrens to make an appointment.  They give me the appointment for up to 5 months, I tell them that it is urgent that if they have a shorter date and they answer me rudely without any empathy that what my son has is not urgent.  There is really a lack of empathy, perhaps it is not urgent for you because he is not your son, for me it is urgent, he is my son and I know it is urgent that he be seen by a health professional.

reviews.author: Lida Nay
reviews.text: If I could rate it ZERO, I would.

reviews.author: Joey
reviews.text: The turn over for employees is extremely high here for a reason. Administration is terrible, residents are terrible, the lack of compassion and empathy for patients families is horrible. I’ve watched doctors panic and create disasters, i would never recommend you to bring your child here. I’d rather fly to another state to seek treatment and care for my child. Avoid avoid at All cost.

reviews.author: Katrina Matthias
reviews.text: I didn't know doctors were still kind,  then we came here.

reviews.author: Caroline Nyagaki
reviews.text: The hospital and all the doctors,nurses, CNA’s and all staff members are amazing. My daughter is a miracle kid and I thank God for giving the children hospital doctors the knowledge that they used to treat my kid. My kid like that hospital even when she is not sick she keep on asking when is her next appointment just to make sure she goes back to the hospital because she got healed there and she was treated very, very nice. I like children’s hospital. May God bless all of you who works there and take good care of our children.

reviews.author: Khadija Qassiem
reviews.text: Love you my hero from iraq ♡

reviews.author: Sumi Rajadurai
reviews.text: Came here for my son's surgery. All the Hosptial staff that we met were really nice, we were well informed about the procedure and post operative care.Food: options aren't that great, some of it was kinda stale.They do have few other services for families on floor 7, the chapel was a peaceful place, to just be.Post operative call/follow up is also something that I valued alot.

reviews.author: Amber Fiedler
reviews.text: My daughter Met with Dr Blessing in the cranio facial dept he was absolutely amazing. He helped calm all of my nerves about my daughter's surgery. Recently we went back for my son who we were worried about and Blessing did everything he could to limit our concerns including ordering a ultrasound for us. My daughter is almost 2 now. Her surgery went perfectly. The whole cranio team did a fantastic job. I could not say anything bad about my visit. Thank you for taking care of my baby girl and myself while I was a mess.

reviews.author: Mari Rodri
reviews.text: Fue un Exelente servicio para mi niño todos muy amables y cariñosos que mi niño se sintió muy confortable ya que es un poco miedoso con los médicos tipico de los nenes 😁 gracias por todo el esfuerzo que hacen por nuestros niños Equipo Seattle children 💕🥰👏👏

reviews.author: Joshua Smith
reviews.text: The best hospital ever!!! This place is so advanced it's not even funny!!! Also, they treat my nephew like gold every time he's here. This is the only hospital I would recommend really. On top of that, they have the nicest nurses who really know their stuff. This place is the best!!!

reviews.author: J H
reviews.text: Thank you for such great care of my little Granddaughter.She was transferred to the Children's hospital and she made a complete turn around after be admitted and now is home with my Son's family.Now they are complete once again.Again thanks to all the staff for an excellent job!

reviews.author: Elie G.
reviews.text: EVERYONE, from check-in, to medical staff, to the older-lady volunteers strolling around the building, are the most nice, warm, thoughtful people ever.

reviews.author: Panda XTG
reviews.text: 10 years I was diagnosed with GBM level 4, I had an egg size tumor in left frontal lobe.I was 18, in drill team, trying out for track, and was very active.It all started with the crossed eyes and waking up every morning, puking from being so dizzy from seeing two of everything.My dad took us to the optometrist and he said I had to go to ER, went there, got an MRI(after taking all my piercings) he said go to Seattle, so there we went.They took out the tumor, and started with pills I could not touch, those literally killed me. I don't know how many GCF shots I got, I got a ton, and they did not work. Then they put me on chemo, radiation, gamma knife.I was doing chemo intravenously in the arms, until got my port!❤️ Radiation smells like rotting pile of bleep. Gamma knife, I can't remember this part, chemo brain.

reviews.author: kedys morale
reviews.text: Delighted with the medical service, they are always attentive to the patient and very good communication, excellent in general.

reviews.author: Catera Mason
reviews.text: They like to cancel appointments the day of or 1 hr before appointment happen 4 times already. Wasted gas and time

reviews.author: Jayde Logan
reviews.text: We had an AWFUL experience at an urgent care. We then went to Seattle Children’s and had an amazing experience. There was a long wait, but they provided blankets and coloring pages for my sons. So attentive and welcoming. Once they saw my son, he was treated quickly and the ligaments in his arm were put back into place. We went in with him crying. He left with a popsicle and with no pain. Thank you all.

reviews.author: Victor Li
reviews.text: Impossible to schedule appointments. Appointments get arbitrarily rescheduled after arrangements have been made. Very difficult to get through to schedulers. Call back service consists of leaving a voice mail. During long wait times their phone line disconnects.

reviews.author: Matthew “narcischizm” Schalow
reviews.text: Always provide exceptional medical service. The only hospital I will take my kids to in Western Washington.

reviews.author: d k
reviews.text: As someone with autism, I did not like how i was being treated during my visit nor do i like the amount i am being charged. During my visit, i was getting glared at, possibly made fun of etc. It was disgusting and made me feel very uncomfortable. I asked doctors about my problems and i thought the help could have been better. I was told by one of the doctors that I would get a call for help about finding a better health insurance because of how S*** everything is. I have been waiting for a phone call and nothing. I owe over $500.00 and before the due date, you dare charge me $300.00 more and without letting me know!? I am not fully paying my bill. The amount of what i paid is what you get.

reviews.author: Norma Arredondo
reviews.text: Por qué no hay discriminación y gracias a ellos vuelven a nacer los niños con una carita sonriente

reviews.author: Brenda Linares
reviews.text: This is supposed to be an emergency location, we brought our daughter here. We arrived at 9:00 pm, it's 11:36 pm and they still haven't called us to see a doctor, I see another person arrive with their son, I didn't wait half an hour and they already sent her to see a doctor. what happen? Aren't all children important? Doesn't everyone deserve to be taken care of? my daughter has a high fever, she is suffering and they do not attend us.

reviews.author: Malia
reviews.text: Drove two hours to get here, traffic was terrible, was 30 minutes late to an appointment, called in before hand and they said they would call back if they couldn’t get us in, never got a call back then when we got there they said they couldn’t take us in for an appointment that should’ve taken 10 min maximum.

reviews.author: Deborah Hou
reviews.text: Eternally waiting, waiting, waiting, until the child recovers on his own.

reviews.author: Rachael Bull
reviews.text: We waited in the ER waiting room for 4 hours without any concern shown. Checked in with reception multiple times and saw many families taken back before my child. I understand different levels of emergency, but the lack of concern/care was something I never expected or have experienced before.

reviews.author: Renee Zmuda
reviews.text: They helped my son use his voice to get the help he needs! Was worth the wait! I promise! The staff and security and more have been so helpful and kind. Offering water or food. While we waited to be seen. The staff here is very polite and sweet! 5-5 stars for me.

reviews.author: mahad idris
reviews.text: Children are suffering in waiting lobby you rather go to urgent care center way faster then coming here ER is very brutal

reviews.author: Ryan Dillon
reviews.text: One star is the minimum, you get a second because you didn't hurt my kids.Now for the negative, billing department is a bunch of hacks...I have a solid insurance plan and you could even work with them to get it right and instead billed me for thousands. Prices are astronomical...$450 for at 10 min consult. Get lost.If your getting referred here, do your research. There are probably other options available to you, but Western WA doctors default to this one, I only assume they hope to one day over charge too.

reviews.author: Kaitlynn Esselborn
reviews.text: Forever grateful for all of the nurses and doctors here at Seattle childrens, you guys are all amazing!

reviews.author: Diana Williams
reviews.text: My child had surgery 07/2022. The stress and worry was pretty intense for me. The Doctors, Nurses, and Staff are God sent and absolutely amazing. We were in excellent hands from beginning to end. My child will need continued services and I will not take her anywhere else. She loves going here. Thank you Seattle Children's Hospital for ALL of your loving support. ❤️

reviews.author: Erik Hart
reviews.text: Great hospital with amazing doctors . Opened doors to help our family that were not possible at other local hospitals.  I feel blessed to have a specialty childrens hospital nearby .

reviews.author: Magy D
reviews.text: Came In at 930pm and it is currently 1:15AM and still have not been called. Staff currently give me a straight answer on how long I'll be waiting.  " hopefully soon they will call you in" this was said 3 times and yet no one called me in. Dissatisfied with this hospital. This is not an emergency room.  Stay away.

reviews.author: Pankaj Sharma
reviews.text: They need to understand the meaning of Emergency, I came to an emergency service at 3:00 AM and I had to wait 2.5 hours inorder see a doctor, my daughter had a fever of 105 she was nauseous,  why do they call this as an emergency service, rather it should be called 24x7 urgent care. If I am paying a premium price for emergency service I don’t think anyone should deserve this kind of service. Seems like I made a mistake coming here.

reviews.author: Robin Goforth
reviews.text: They are my superheroes.  The Dr's. Nurse's and staff are all so kind. And have brought me peace during the days I worry the most.

reviews.author: J Huang
reviews.text: My 8-year-old daughter unfortunately had appendicitis on the day of boarding a cruise from Seattle to Alaska, and had to go through a surgery at the Seattle Children’s hospital. We were obviously so worried about her health, and disappointed at the same time that she couldn’t board the ship.  However, an exceptional level of empathy, kindness and professionalism demonstrated by Dr J. Meehan and his medical team put my daughter and myself at ease throughout the surgery process. We felt so blessed to have him and his medical team treat and care for her. Everyone was so nice, friendly and professional, treating us like their own family members! Our family really appreciate Dr Meehan being such a caring, thoughtful and compassionate doctor during our time of need! Thank you Seattle Children’s Hospital for making this experience wonderful!

reviews.author: charlene avamalefono
reviews.text: I dont like the commute and also it is hell checking in! Have to go to the 6th floor to stand in line outthe door to go to 8th where it is crowded and receptionist cant hear you throught he glass. I absolutely HATE it here

reviews.author: Kristen Fisher
reviews.text: After nearly 18 years of taking my severely disabled child here with at times damaging results - I would implore you to look elsewhere for care.  This place has lost empathy and results. Apparently after they pass you around to other people who have no clue how to help they terminate you - this place is the saddest joke - I used to have such hope but after the last dr sent a letter saying  ‘sorry moving on good luck’ (many such letters) I guess the egos win.  They made my daughter worse with little or no help.  No miracles here

reviews.author: De’Lacia Nance
reviews.text: This hospital is literally like a home to me and my family they have token care of my brother sense he was a newborn.

reviews.author: V S
reviews.text: Super disappointed and angry post visit. We ended up going to Seattle childrens due to lack of appointments and a reference from my kids pediatrician and I regret going to them. Highly mismanaged facility - people walking  around without masks. We were seated in a casting room for an hour with random folks walking in and out and when I asked the check in person for the delay reason he simply responded the doctor is busy and won't know when he will be done. This was for a pre scheduled appointment. When I said this was unacceptable his response was - do you want to cancel? I am appalled at the lack of empathy or any kind of concern for a parent and kid. I will not recommend them to anyone. Also, we were asked for symptoms and masks at every checkpoint but their own physicians were checking patients in flimsy barely there masks. I was very uncomfortable throughout the visit. This is a very badly run facility (it did not feel like a hospital).

reviews.author: P DM
reviews.text: ZERO STARS....If you are a black person whether you have insurance or not..STAY AWAY FROM Seattle Children's. Their issues of discrimination against black families is still raging, plus no respect or communication with waiting patients whose appointment time they have delayed.Twice now I had an appointment and still had to wait over an hour after check in.Even if you have an appointment, you end up waiting like in ER. Had a 940am appointment, arrived at 925am and did not see the doctor until 11am.Second time, we had a surgery scheduled for  230pm, we waited til 3pm and noone was telling us anything. . Then i told them we were leaving if I did not get an exact eta and was told it could be another hour. This iseven though my 4 year old had not eaten since 6am for the procedure and it was now 348pm and her original appointment was 230p.When I asked why the wait I was was told that a "more important case was put ahead of ours". Apparently some lives matter more at Children's. We left without the procedure.

reviews.author: Consuelo Villavicencio
reviews.text: Todo el personal muy amable

reviews.author: Charlotte Alexander
reviews.text: My child and I went on a Friday night.   It took about 2 hours to be seen by the doctor.  My child broke their arm.   And another 1 hour for the x-ray and then the cast to be set.  While it felt long at in the moment… and we weren’t a serious case, everyone was professional and helpful.

reviews.author: jaquelinne lomeli
reviews.text: Worst experience ever!!  I had to leave took forever to check my child!

reviews.author: Enid Duncan
reviews.text: My grandson has autism. I made several phone calls and only machines answered. I miss appointment on 08/01/22 I tried

reviews.author: Gina
reviews.text: I'm originally from Miami, so I don't think no health care or anything can outdo that. But Seattle Children's Hospital is an amazing hospital that I have been to, and it was honestly such a good experience. My son was admitted for surgery yesterday, and they have cared for him with so much love; I can't even explain how wonderful they have been. The nurses, doctors, and staff members have been amazing with my son. My family and I drove a little over an hour and a half, and it was worth it. The level of security and organization here is priceless. I met several nurses, but one that stood out the most was "Sammie" omg. I loved her; she was sweet and made me feel comfortable. She takes her job seriously and is very dedicated to the patients. I know there are many more nurses who were just like Sammie and were great, but there was one that blew me away. My son immediately connected with her, and the fact she stayed overtime is commendable. Thank you all so much for your hospitality, grace, and professionalism. I pray God continues blessing this institution and all the lovely people who work here. May God continue to bless you all.

reviews.author: Angela H
reviews.text: Today we went and saw Jacob Ross for PT and he was fantastic! The receptionist also remembered us from last time and provided coloring sheets for my daughter who had asked for pokemon ones a few months back. The fact that she remembered really touched us and to top it off Ross gave our kiddo a pokemon card pack after PT. Absolutely made her day and ours. Thank you all for being such great humans!

reviews.author: Solito
reviews.text: The Emergency department is a joke. They are understaffed and it shows. They don’t take the time or show that they even care. My daughter and wife were at the ED for over 5 hours. They did nothing for my daughter who is still in excruciating pain. Sent her away as if they didn’t want to help her. I don’t see how they can keep running the ED like this. Someone is going to get hurt or even killed due to their complacency and they can care less. Seattle childrens again dropping the ball at the expense of my child. Horrible establishment wasting innocent child’s time just for the sake of money. I hope their bill come due.

reviews.author: David Shipley
reviews.text: I'd like to separate my review into two parts. If you only care about doctors and medical service, just read part 1 and call it 5 stars.1. Every doctor was understanding, great bedside manner, consoling and supportive. They knew what they were doing and helped us to understand.2. The consistency in staff outside of doctors is very off. Came into ER with our child and had multiple people ask us if we needed food/drink/comfort and never returned with what was promised. Not once, several times.Room we waited in for 5 hours had 2 office chairs my wife was supposed to breastfeed in. No pillows available, just a thin blanket.Told us we would both be able to stay overnight with our child, at 7:30 pm. After leaving us alone until 12:30 am other than checking in and not delivering services, they told us only one of us could stay. Hotel unbookable at that hour.Once my wife was in the room, asked for pain medication for child 3 times before it was delivered. There was no discussion, they agree it was needed and just didn't bring it.These places make money hand over fist, or else I'm paying someone else a fortune. Invest a bit less in colorful, whimsical fox paintings on the walls and a bit more consistency in staffing and protocols please.

reviews.author: Amelia Watt
reviews.text: ENT and other specific specialists, along with the 90% of the nursing staff make it a potential great choice. The facilities are great in the sense they are clean,  but logistically laid out poorly.  If you're here for an extended period of time, it's not a good choice though. Don't expect to sleep and you'd probably have a better conversation with a wall than with the management here. Specifically, the Patient Family Relations Group are full of liars and pretend to be an advocate for you when you're trying to do everything possible for your child's health, but they are like an HR department for the company,  they will say whatever sounds good at the time and when you feel like you can trust them, you end up feeling as though you've been deceived, lied to, and that no help is in the foreseeable future. The specialists are what you want for your children, but the management are all about the bottom line and they have no real interest in the patients or their families. If I hadn't been here for months now, with a strong history of knowledge between the ENT team and my daughter,  and if I had known more about this place (I just moved here less than a year ago), I would have very likely gone somewhere else. I could go on and on, but it really doesn't make a difference with them. They honestly don't care (they being management, not the actual specialists, which the ENT group is amazing). I have been calling around for pediatric ENT specialists, so if anyone knows of someone who is amazing, I'm praying for a better experience and to get out of here.

reviews.author: Kelsey Jacobson
reviews.text: Cannot say enough how amazing this hospital and the staff is. My daughter is a patient here and every single time we are here we are treated with so much care and respect. So grateful for her neurology team. These employees are simply the best.

reviews.author: Caitlyn Nilson
reviews.text: I can’t say enough about our experience at the children’s ER. Upon arrival my son and I were greeted by a nurse immediately while my husband checked in. Even though any ER visit is usually a long one, staff was so attentive and wasted no time helping our little guy. The surgeons and staff in the surgery recovery unit were equally amazing. Everyone was above and beyond compassionate, thorough and informative with us every step of the way for what was already a traumatic experience. If we ever have to take our son to the ER again, this will be the only place we go.

reviews.author: Dawna Cunningham
reviews.text: I have not had a problem at any of my sons appointments

reviews.author: Brandy Fowler
reviews.text: Absolutely atrocious service from craniofacial medicine. It is impossible to get ahold of anyone there for scheduling or rescheduling. The referral process took several weeks. There is no prioritization process for kids that are about to become “too old” for treatment. We have been trying since March to get an appointment. They cancelled on us the same day as our appointment and couldn’t reschedule us for three weeks. My child is no longer eligible for treatment due to these delays. They have absolutely failed him.

reviews.author: Jacob McCarter
reviews.text: All the staff we've worked with so far have been friendly and answered any questions we have, whether it be radiology or the dietary. Really quick and on time appointments too. Not much waiting around.

reviews.author: Ashley Heether
reviews.text: Everyone here is super friendly. They make sure you understand everything that's happening before it happens. Hospital is very clean and organized.

reviews.author: Dolores Stewart
reviews.text: I was a patient here when I was 10 years old they fixed my legs  so i coud walk for the first time I am now 58 not only did they take care of my body but also helped the mind God bless this hospital

reviews.author: Dogz Tied TV
reviews.text: It was good either than the fact Curtis Carlock is a terrible doctor and he should be fired

reviews.author: fabian cantu
reviews.text: Such great staff all around! Very polite and they take great care of you and your child!

reviews.author: Cathy Fish
reviews.text: Seattle Children's is the worst!  It is impossible to get appointments and when you finally do, they cancel on you.  How is there no other options for pediatric endocrinology?  My child is not getting the care she needs to manage her diabetes because of their lack of doctors and clinics.

reviews.author: Haiyan Chen
reviews.text: They just let my kid sleep at SCH which I agree because she had no problem at all.  But but but SCH charged us over 2000 dollars for sleeping several hours at their room!!!!! The price is after the discount!!! 1. My kid had no problem. 2. Even though assume she had problem, do you need 2000 dollars to do the evaluation? 3. You just let her sleep in your room instead of in her own bed in her own room, what the $2000 come from? 4. We asked for breakfast, but never come before we leave the hospital.5. Thank you that you didn't try to persuade us believe my normal kid is abnormal. You are professional at this point. Thanks God, at least you didn't abuse medicine.

reviews.author: Makayla
reviews.text: Beautiful hospital and the staff was nice for the most part. We had to come here to visit the ENT. His name was Dr. Manning. The doctor was rude and seemed to not believe me about my daughters symptoms. He kept saying "If" these things were happening. And then he also kept going on and on about how  girl and boy patients were different and how his boy patients didn't want to do things. I was really disappointed because we drove over an hour to see this guy.

reviews.author: Ali N
reviews.text: Thanks for helping us in emergency

reviews.author: blair m
reviews.text: Dr. Boos was an answer to our prayers. Our 3 yr old sone developed a fungus on his head that was cut open (when it shouldn't have been) by a NP. We took him to our local derm (we are not from Seattle) and they did the best that they knew how- but unfortunately they didn't know how to help his head heal. It was very far for us to travel, but it was worth it. In 2 visits, with many phone calls & emails back and forth Dr. Boos was able to help heal our sons head. He knew things that our local derms (we saw 2) didn't know. His knowledge of medicines for children was amazing.Things that stick out to me about Dr. Boos;*He is honest*He listens to parents and the kids* He is not a "know it all"* I felt he truly cares about the well being of our son*He is willing to research for your child* He is kind.

reviews.author: Savannah Melissa Flores (savvy)
reviews.text: I am currently going through the most frustrating time right about now. I have been thinking of ways to type in a way other families are aware and can understand as a mother of a muticomplexed baby who's getting taken from me for things I cannot control, I have been dealing with harassment, emotional destress, called an unfit mother who neglects her world, pride and joy and also told and have been seeing the way I am being treated as his biological mother who was blocked on the MyChart from being able to view my own son's medical portal. I have been treated horribly and disrespected in ways no parent or parents should ever be treated like they aren't apart of their childs care team , neglected to be told information like, changes in medication their child is taking, nutrition changes, meetings with the child's surgical care team and discussing about the child without the parents made aware or without any consent on what's being talked and with who. I have witnessed the disrespect these nurse practitioners are showing and had to let another person I don't know have classes done on without my approval and he is a fragile baby. Someone please that views these make thos this be known as I am currently dealing with this whole my son's admitted is the hardest thing I've ever had to deal with and iam not happy about the situation that's takin place and it's your staff that's betraying my trust when your employees were the ones that knew our son's previous hospital that we had complications with because of not caring for my son's health that's fragile and for this happening and for my son's father to be told he doesn't know his son and we are not medically certified to be his parents and care for our son when we have done nothing but what was directed and to be told I am no longer my son's mother when my name is on his birth certificate. My son is not going to be treated any different, I would appreciate help because they are tearing my family apart and ignoring my feelings and my saying his medical needs. Please and thank you

reviews.author: Sophiaa L.
reviews.text: Dr. Manning is a very very good doctor/surgeon. Thank you to nursing staff and Dr. Manning for taking very good care of my son during surgery very GREATFUL and THANKFUL. 💐💐

reviews.author: Nicole R-E
reviews.text: This is a great place. The doctors that I have encountered with are amazing. The stay was nice as well meeting the other doctors. The only thing I don't like is a shared room situation. I think it's odd but it's what has to happen. Clinic is great too.

reviews.author: Analisa Magnano
reviews.text: I went here for 11 days in order to stabilize during a low part during my ed however the doctors were fairly strict and set me up for failure along my path to recovery. Some doctors also did not seem they knew how handle my illness and it seemed they were more interested in treating the heart rate than the person.

reviews.author: Amanuel Kahssai
reviews.text: Unlike my usual optimism, I am leaving this negative review because Seattle Children’s hooked me with this below “low rated” health equipment supplier company called Byram Health care.With a child’s T1D diagnosis, I was introduced to ongoing dependency to diabetic supplies. The only supplier I was offered at the time of diagnosis was Byram and I started ordering from them. After five years of terrible experience with Byram that negatively impacted my son’s health, I am leaving my review of  Seattle Children to publicly ask them to loose tie with this incompetent health care supplier company called Byram.Without going to PHI a lot, my experience includes interruption of mailing a life sustaining supplies with no communication, being told supplies were mailed to me while they weren’t (multiple times each quarter), hunging up phone when I asked to speak with supervisor, or the usual “supervisor will call you later” and they will never call.Seattle Children’s please verify your vendors before referring to families,  because families trust your reputation.Byram deservingly is rated “1” in BBB and “1” at Yelp.

reviews.author: Kiarash
reviews.text: Very Bad service, today I and my little son, waited from 4:30 till now(10 pm-over 5 hours) they  are not check in us and the Nurse told me you have to wait 2 more hours.Disappointed children hospital 👎🏿I thought at least in your hospital care about children and their health , but you are same as all other businesses.

reviews.author: Ashleigh Albert
reviews.text: My child spent about 543 days at SCH and I would not recommend them to anyone for any inpatient stay or any services that may lead to them being admitted. The NICU was absolutely horrible. They treated parents very poorly. Refused to call me for rounds and I found out multiple diagnoses weeks or months after they had been found because no one bothered to call and tell us. (A hernia, volume loss in the brain, GERD, etc.) We were at a smaller NICU before SCH that was absolutely wonderful and had great communication, and to switch to SCH who clearly did not care if we were involved in our child's care and decision making, or even kept educated on it, was absolutely traumatic. This was not one Resident or Attending, this was months of this treatment from multiple Residents, Attendings, and nurses. We requested primary nurses but that didn't happen, my child had a different nurse every 4 - 8 hours for 3 months in the NICU. Physical Therapist Angela Fritz, and one traveling nurse were the only staff members that brightened our NICU stay and that I can say we enjoyed working with. Angela is incredibly positive, confident, and does a wonderful job including parents and communicating effectively.The PICU was better as far as communication goes, however staff seemed afraid of our child. He had a tracheostomy at that point and we were allowed to pick him up, bathe him, etc without help, but it was clear the nurses were afraid and uncomfortable with us doing so. Because of their fear he was left in bed alone watching movies for at leat 20 hours a day for his entire 11.5 month stay in the PICU, minus the days we were present to get him out of bed and into his swing or activity chair. He also did not have a primary nurse for any of his approximately 11.5 months in the PICU. We got a Continuity Attending in the PICU who followed his care more closely, went to BPD Rounds (we were not allowed to attend, we tried,) and advocated for us. Dr. Emily Berkman was our Continuity Attending and she was great to work with. In the PICU and on the "Floor" nurses were extremely loud at 3am shift change and would often wake me up in the room with the door shut at this time. They also choose to schedule things (in the PICU and on the Floor) in a way where they are bothering your child all night long, every hour or so, even with tasks that could easily be grouped and done earlier or later.The "Pulmonary Floor" nurses are MUCH more experienced and confident. They trusted our training and abilities and the 3.5 or so months we spent there were the first time we were truly allowed to care for our child without someone hovering over us or interrupting constantly. It was also the first time the Pulmonologists came to speak with us semi-regularly, even though he had been closely followed by the Pulmonology team for about 14.5 months there. (I had seen a Pulmonologist less than 5 times during that time.) Dr. Amanda Striegl is a wonderful Pulmonologist. She was much more confident than any doctor, resident or Attending, that we met during our stay. Dr. Laurie Eldrege was also very understanding and great to work with. We had a few long talks about communication and continuity of care and both of these Pulmonologists were very receptive to my criticism and understanding of my frustration.During our time at SCH I requested a second opinion from another hospital twice. The first time they tried to tell me they don't do second opinions, then they offered to present his case at a conference that was then postponed due to covid, then 3 months after I initially asked with no progress, I had to contact a Social Worker to advocate for me and get a second opinion. The 2nd opinion gave them critical info that moved my child's progress forward immensely. The 2nd time I wanted a second opinion SCH had been telling me my child would be inpatient at least 6 more months. I made them get a 2nd opinion and he was safely discharged about a month later. Horrible experience, would not recommend for anything inpatient or that could get you admitted.

reviews.author: Marti Louther
reviews.text: My daughter was born with a disability. Needless to say we have spent A LOT of time here. With a very few exceptions (like one, and it’s been 18 years) every single doctors has been excellent!! Every single nurse and support staff are incredible!! It is a gem. Thank you for all you do for all children, and particularly for those children who need more and specialized care.

reviews.author: Vyktorya Ruth
reviews.text: The staff was very professional and super kind. Not only did they answer all of my questions I had, they took amazing care of my daughter and they also were very caring of me as a parent offering me snacks and drinks. I absolutely love this hospital

reviews.author: Sgt T
reviews.text: Never go there.  Their staff will make assumptions over half heard conversations apologize  and then do it again. 2 visits later

reviews.author: Phanindra Garimella (Phani)
reviews.text: One of the best among hospital for kids in the US. Entire Staff including the Doctors, nurses and administrative staff are really courteous. They took care of my daughter who was having issues with developmental disabilities including several visits and emergency.i really want to thank them for all the help and support they gave us since last few months.The only problem is getting outpatient appointments which will run for months and depends totally on the speciality. I recommend Seattle Children's hospital for the parents who are looking for any type medical help including emergency, urgent care and well child check-up (this depends on the requirements though).

reviews.author: Ashare Goosby
reviews.text: Cherese pullum has been a big provoking factor of a issue dealing with my child being with my exe false cps reports making my exe disown kids that loved him dearly because she wanted to move in with him she is really unprofessional and no help to children none whatsoever I will have be contacting a lawyer for her next

reviews.author: Mr. Mark L.
reviews.text: A referral for Psychiatric services for my daughter was was sent to Children's Hospital on Sandpoint on February 26, 2021 from my daughters physician. The day after the referral was sent they informed me theres a waiting list.  So I remained patient. Ive since heard nothing back from them. Its now October. I called yesterday and they said they closed the referral. They claimed my doctor never responded to a request for more information, but that was a lie, as our doctor has record of faxing it back to them the day after they requested.  We had it re-sent and Ive still heard nothing back after several phone calls, leaving voice messages, and getting the run-around.  Would I receive this type of services if my child wasn't a child of color???? During these difficult times, these services are desperately needed more the ever.  This is disturbing, neglectful, and unacceptable from Children's Hospital Psychiatric Behavioral division.  My Doctor has had to refer me to a different facility due to Children's Hospitals lack of care, negligence, and unprofessionalism.  I am looking in to taking this matter to the media.

reviews.author: Jillian Diner
reviews.text: Once we were admitted to the emergency department, they saw my son quickly.  All the doctors and nurses were really great - communicated with us, made sure we were part of the decision making process, taking care of my son during a scary time.  I'm so glad we don't live too far from a great health resource for my kids like Seattle Children's!!

reviews.author: Tracy Valentine
reviews.text: Kind caring compassionate organized informative thorough thank you so much for your time understanding and overall quality Care excellent teamwork

reviews.author: Amy Mimi
reviews.text: I came here along side my little cousin who had to get admitted through the Emergency Room. Everybody from the front desk to the back; security, nurses, resident, attending, were beyond excellent and had the most amazing patient care. They checked on us every so often which was very sweet. The hospital is really clean, and the room we are in are clean and they are taking all the precautions. Thank you SCH !

reviews.author: Billie Swanson
reviews.text: They saved my daughters life when another hospital had given up. We only trust SCH and travel there for every appointment.

reviews.author: Chelsey True
reviews.text: Our 6-month-old son recently had to have an emergency surgery here. I cannot stress how attentive, compassionate and understanding each person we worked with was towards us.  Dr. Otjen and Dr. Perez, in Radiology, were wonderful. Dr. Rice-Townsend is an incredibly kind surgeon with great bedside manner. Dr. Meehan is wonderful to work with as well and is very attentive and has a great way of explaining things. I wish I could remember all the nurses as well. Each one we interacted with was great.

reviews.author: Karima Robles
reviews.text: I was nervous to bring my son here after reading some of the bad reviews but everyone was super nice, from the people checking us in and also the random nurses we saw in the hospital after we got lost they stopped to help us even though they were busy and Dr Deen and his staff are truly amazing they put us at ease and really made us feel comfortable also the ultrasound techs were great. I recommend bringing your children here although I hope you never need to.

reviews.author: Dulce Villa Martinez
reviews.text: Loved it! I went there just a year ago for mental health reasons but I went to the pbmu ( psychiatry behavioral medicine unit) and the staff are so nice and compassionate I was diagnosed with severe depression and generalized anxiety disorder then I finally realized what was bothering me my care team helped me along my week I was there definitely recommend you take your children there

reviews.author: Vicky
reviews.text: I've been to this hospital since my daughter was admitted a week ago, I did not have the best experience as a guest,  the staff at the PBMU & patient floor unit was very unhelpful except for a few such as the front desk lady I came to the first time to check-in was very helpful & friendly to me. The rest of the hospital staff was not willing to offer assistance, I was so lost at first I had to go out of my way to ask the laundry cleaning lady to help me find the floor /room I was suppose to be in they ignored me so I found another employee to help me find how to get to the floor my daughter was on. Be sure to ask for a map or your stuck on your own.

reviews.author: J.L. G. (Jay)
reviews.text: Great place love it. ❤

reviews.author: Joanna Kumar
reviews.text: Our son’s heart failure and transplant team has been nothing short of amazing and we are looking forward to the next 18+ years with them.Our nurses in the CICU and on the medical floor created the warmest and most empowering experience they could as we were inpatient for 6 months.COVID was a pain, but they worked with us as a family in many ways. The nurses and doctors would provide a consistent experience between dad and myself. Therapy would often come twice a day so they could work with the two of us while we were on rotation.With all of the challenges that were presented, we always felt reassured and hopeful.We’ve been readmitted a couple times since discharge and still love being with our friends at Seattle Childrens.

reviews.author: Juno Choi
reviews.text: Mission driven professionals and great facility. Grateful to have this hospital in our community knowing kids in trouble will get best care by the compassionate team.

reviews.author: Karen Lund
reviews.text: Thank you for taking such good care of my grand daughter, Summer today. She had a perforated appendix and was in so much pain. She's still in recovery and I hope to talk with her soon. God bless nurses and doctors everywhere but especially Seattle today. Thank you 😊 💓 ☺ 💗

reviews.author: JayKB
reviews.text: My granddaughter had surgery for a spinal tumor that wound around her entire spine. The doctors were great. The aftercare... basically non-existent! She had to wear diapers, which to her were bad enough. After a bowel movement that had fecal matter clear up onto the incision, she was left lying for many hours in it. The nurses did not bath her for days on end, nor were her sheets changed. The care giving parent was out of money because of all the problems of getting her there. The hospital said they would provide meals. Which they did...one per day. Instead of the nurses giving her oral meds, it was left to the parent. After over a week, the parent was too exhausted, and the nurses only complained he needed to do more. While his daughter was left unbathed and in filthy bedding. This hospital is supposed to be one of, if not the best, children's hospital in the United States. We sure didn't see it!

reviews.author: Dan Gamman
reviews.text: Thank God for Seattle Childrens. I feel like they really care about my son. Taking a child to a hospital is always a trying experience. The wonderful staff makes the experience bearable. We would be lost without them. Thank you for all you do.

reviews.author: Ashleigh Correll
reviews.text: My child initially spent 18 months here. For about 16 months of that, they left him alone in bed watching TV for at least 20 hours a day. The NICU was absolutely awful and wouldn't keep you apprised of your child's care and new diagnosis no matter how much you begged the doctors, nurses, left big notes on the white board, etc. I found out about hernias, volume loss in his brain, and Cerebral Palsy weeks or months after initial diagnosis when someone casually mentioned it, assuming I had been told when he was initially diagnosed. The culture there is awful. Then the PICU was slightly better, but they were all terrified of my child. It became clear the doctors and specialty team didn't know how to help my child progress medically, and after three months of asking for a second opinion from another hospital I had to throw a fit and get Social Work involved to help me make it happen. He made loads of progress as soon as the other hospital's recommendations were put into place. My child is medically complex, and they continued to change and add to the list of things that needed to be checked off before going home. Every time we took a step closer,, they would add another requirement they had never mentioned before. Now that we have been home for 9 months I am fully aware that I am way more capable of caring for my child than any nurse or RT at SCH. We have since had emergencies in the ER as a result of SCH staff not doing their jobs correctly. They are terrified of him, have absolutely no concept of his abilities, maybe because they leave him in bed all day. They have no faith in us parents even though they trained us. They hold children for months and refuse to release them without "adequate home nursing" but won't come out and say what that means. They recently left my child in the ER for 5 hours with no food or water with his feeding tube hanging out of his stomach, held in place by diapers, while they investigated a handful of minor bruises including 18 xrays that showed no fractures. Then they admitted my child after telling multiple witnesses that there was no medical reason to hold him, and refused to release him for FIVE DAYS. Edit to add: they did not discharge him until we made it clear we had hired attorneys, knew that there was no law requiring nursing, and that we didn't think they had the legal right to hold him. How much money do you think they will make from our private insurance and Medicaid for that 5 day stay that had no medical reason behind it? They also expect us to return 2 weeks from the ER visit for 18 more xrays, when he had no fractures the first time. They have already made over $1 million off of my hild and are trying to milk him for as much private insurance and Medicaid money as they can get.

reviews.author: Carmellitia Speredowich
reviews.text: Hi, I give this hospital a 0/5 stars, but it won’t let me put that.  The nurses always forgot to bring me what I need, they were also late most of the time. I mean like an hour sometimes 2 hours late. There were rude nurses. They would ask personal questions. Also, the doctors asked questions that had nothing to do with my recovery. The doctors also lied. They said everything is fine with me and I’m all healthy but still keep me in. Seems like they just want money.

reviews.author: Angela Rico
reviews.text: They killed my baby, they never gave me an answer that was what happened, terrible service, I do not recommend that they go to that hospital.

reviews.author: Walter Champlin
reviews.text: My son was born with Esophageal Atresia in Montana. He was medflighted to Seattle Childrens Hospital and had a 6 month stay. They are one of a select few hospitals that can work with patients like my son. Because of my son's specific and rare birth defect they had to do an experimental surgery which was tailored specifically to him. Seattle Childrens Hospital allowed my son a second chance at a normal life with a working esophagus I cannot recommend this Hospital enough. The staff, building, organization, etc... all of it is the highest quality. The people here are miracle workers. Rest assured your child is in the best of care here.

reviews.author: Michael Gutierrez
reviews.text: Just like most medical establishment. You are just a number... no one is more Important then their pompous self’s and if they mess up guess what... the client pays for it in time, re covid testing... etc. I would never recommend taking any infant here despite their (children’s hospital) attempt to market their way (with lots of money) into our lives.

reviews.author: Luv Barrett
reviews.text: We come about every 3 week and we are so grateful to the amazing staff and medical professionals who care for our loved ones. Every time we've come has been a positive experience regardless of the scary situation that brings us here.I JUST saw an amazing interaction between a young patient and a medical team member that made me smile. The team member introduced herself to the young patient and wanted to explain the procedure so she would not be scared. She was so amazing and caring and kind and I'm so impressed with her demeanor. I wish I knew her name because she is most definitely an amazing person who cares deeply about her patients.

reviews.author: Eric Mansell
reviews.text: Dr. Susarla and team are miracle workers. A year ago, our 18mo old daughter’s life was in their hands. This is a world class cranio squad. We cannot thank you enough for giving our daughter a chance to live a “normal” life. Thank you for the care and compassion for your patients and their parents. Thank you for the years of hard work and dedication to perfect your skills. Wishing you all the best, Aria is doing amazing 🍾😁!

reviews.author: Leah Wright
reviews.text: My daughter is a frequent patient, and has been for the last 7 years. We put complete trust in this hospital and all the staff.

reviews.author: Heather
reviews.text: The few times I had to bring my children here, the nurses were extremely rude. I dont appreciate attitude and people thinking they are better than others just because they are a nurse. A children's hospital is not good place for a person with a bad attitude to be.

reviews.author: X X (N/A)
reviews.text: I was held here for mental instability. I went in feeling minor suicidal feelings, I exited feeling extremely suicidal. 0/10 food was bad

reviews.author: rajorshi sen
reviews.text: Went to the emergency unit of Seattle Children's in Seattle. Since, it was pandemic time , there were clear instructions that only one parent should be allowed to go inside. They were very considerate to let both me and my wife accompany our daughter who was ill . We were let in with the condition that only one of us can accompany our kid to the laboratories.Starting from the office stuff, receptionist  , nurses and doctors everybody was kind not only to the kid but to us too.The doctors were patient to hear us out , patiently explained each and every test and the course of the treatment. I am thoroughly impressed at the same time I regret that they cannot be my kid's primary care because they either work for specialized treatment or in emergency.

reviews.author: Ginger Herron
reviews.text: We love everything about Seattle Childrens!

reviews.author: Alexis Harste
reviews.text: My son was referred to the Endocrinologist at Seattle Children’s, after battling his primary doctors for several months in what could be wrong with him. After meeting with the team here, the Doctor ordered one last test just in case - even after we provided answers that didn’t necessarily fit possibly needing that last blood test. I am forever grateful they did though! They discovered very high numbers in a Celiac Disease blood test and had us schedule an appt with the Gastroenterologist at Seattle Children’s who confirmed the diagnosis through an endoscopy. Since this diagnosis beginning of March, 2020, my son has grown 7 inches and 35 pounds - in 8 months! This has truly helped him both physically and mentally and we are forever grateful for the doctors at Seattle Children ❤️ Thank you so much for forever changing the course of his life and for listening to our concerns, when his primary doctors wouldn’t 🙏

reviews.author: Nadiya
reviews.text: Doctors and stuff are friendly. Child's Life workers makes a big difference for child's experience in the hospital. The post surgery recovery department's walls, flors and baseboards looks dirty. One of the sink in the room is draining poorly. TV, drapes, and furniture (including patient bed) are very old. Hope, Seattle Children's will renovates it eventually. iPad in the room is greatly appreciated! Main concern, that some caregivers, who are entering patient's room, are not wearing face mask correctly: their noses and mouths are totally visible. Wish this policy was more strict. At least, for patients, who are taking chemotherapy and really cannot afford to be exposed to viruses, in the era, when Covid-19 is sweeping across the country.

reviews.author: Ssfont
reviews.text: So very thankful for the staff at this hospital. Everything was above and beyond what I expected. My son and I really appreciate all the hard work and dedication.

reviews.author: emeila praseutsihn
reviews.text: Been in and out of this hospital for the past 4-5 years. Good care, and wonderful nurses that understands you or your child.

reviews.author: Martin Barragan
reviews.text: Buen hospital para todos los niños enfermos

reviews.author: Jordan Burgess
reviews.text: My wife and I took the day off work for an appointment for my son. We traveled over from Eastern Washington just to find out that they are only allowing one parent into the appointment with the children. I was told I had to wait outside of the hospital after we arrived. If you have an appointment here you better call before had to make sure both parents are allowed inside during the appointment. We arrived around 3:30pm; hand the keys off the the FREE valet parking. Come back back out to the parking lot two hours later only to find out that they close the valet parking at 5pm so I called the hospital to find out where my keys and vehicle were located. Well sir you have to go to the first floor and wait in line for your keys at the front desk then go walk around the massive parking lot for 30 minutes hitting your panic button on your key fob to locate your vehicle. What a mess! Very disappointed in the customer service and the way they do business.

reviews.author: Desiree Dutt
reviews.text: If I could give no stars, I would. This organization has become the puppy mill of pediatric endocrinology.  My daughter has been diabetic for the last 8 years. We moved here three years ago and it has been a nightmare every visit. First, we have not had a consistent doctor the entire 3 years- due to them moving from location to location. Oh, and forgive me for needing to stay close to my house since I do work, have other children and responsibilities- driving to downtown is not an option.  Secondly, no one completes paperwork. I am currently dealing with my insurance company and Omnipod. NO ONE completed the medical necessity paperwork or turned in the clinic notes- that were requested 3 times prior to MAY 2020. The medical necessity MUST be completed every year???? How do you not do this? Is it my job to tell you how to complete paperwork for every tiny detail? Why force me to come in 4 times a year and NEVER COMPLETE the paperwork. It makes no sense- when you are diabetic you need to get prescriptions and/or medical devices in a timely manner.  Also, it appears they can't word clinic notes correctly, because they don't review my daughter's paperwork correctl7 and just send in a stock form- so my daughter was denied her Omnipod- which she has had for over 5 years, because the clinic notes were not specific on what device was being used and for how long- so the insurance wanted to move her to MEDTRONIC! Are you kidding me- how hard is it know what device your patient is using?  Don't even get me started on the billing- if you actually look at the billing codes- which I have went over with the insurance company- they pretty much charge you to go to the actual building (building fee), to sit with the doctor, charge you to have the doctor read the data that I brought in, charge you to take the A1c, charge you to tell you the A1c- and I still pay my 50 dollar co-pay! It's amazing scam.  I can't not tell you enough- if you are new to this town- go to Everett Clinic- find another location that will partner with you and help you. These people have no idea what they are doing. It's absolutely painful. I am now just waiting once again to get through this round of medical necessity paperwork and I am moving on- I can' t do it anymore.

reviews.author: Mo
reviews.text: Worst we have ever seen. Very unreliable staff. We needed an emergency appointment and pediatrician sent them referrals tons of times and specified the necessity for my kid to be seen urgently, and they denied us for 3 weeks to schedule an appointment. All response we got is that we do not meet their criteria. They even refused to say what is the criteria. It's so sad that they are the only option in Seattle and my family is lost now where we can go next.

reviews.author: Danette Grace Wells
reviews.text: Caring and helpful staff

reviews.author: Sol Henderson
reviews.text: Total nightmare. They falsified logs n stole my baby. I have serious douts on the professionalism of this hospital n staff.

reviews.author: Becky Clendenen
reviews.text: Terrible! After waiting a year we get there the check in person is so short and rude then the Opthomologist is in and out lf the room like 8 times so impersonal she spent a total of like 9 minutes tops then tells me her nurse will be in. My grand daughter got a new pair of glasses and can't even see with them. Frustrated doesn't even cover it!

reviews.author: Ellie Kunis
reviews.text: Discharge time is horribleIt's like they dont care about and your child

reviews.author: Wilfrido Martinez
reviews.text: Nos atendieron muy bien por allá todo muy bien organizado y excelente cuidado con sus pacientes y gracias a Dios todo salió bien con nuestro hijo en la unica visita gracias Seattle Children's

reviews.author: Tay Waltier
reviews.text: I was in the hospital for about a month with an illness and lost lots of my memory, and they helped me and they kept helping me improve in many ways for many things.

reviews.author: caitlyn harkness
reviews.text: Our toddler broke her arm and we were transported here from a smaller community After midnight 3/13 advised Childrens would be the best people to surgically repair her break. Every single person we encountered was amazing. They're kind, professional, prompt, and 100000% there to make the children they see as comfortable as possible while treating them like a normal little human being. They explained things to my child every step of the way and we're gracious and accommodating every time I had panic attacks or emotional breakdowns due to stress and lack of sleep. Hands down the best hospital experience I have encountered after years of ER visits and surgeries I went through as a child and young adult.

reviews.author: Anatoliy M
reviews.text: Working here as a contractor is pretty cool. People particularily medical staff are nice and friendly. The hospital does a great job at providing care for its patients and puts patients first always. It has a lot of great places to just sit and relax.

reviews.author: Julian Robertson
reviews.text: Excellent experience at the abumbant ED nourishment stations. 10/10 most def would go again. Ps: Casey the accountant is the cat's pajamas.

reviews.author: Zach K
reviews.text: Beautiful hospital and generally good staff. However, they are not responsive to anything outside of normal procedure. My son had pneumonia and we went to Overlake in Bellevue. The doctor there wanted my son to be observed overnight, and Overlake doesn't have bed for kids. So he sent us to Children's with a packet of tests and a call to the staff there to get us in bed and observe us. Well, Children's put us through the exact same emergency room procedures as if we were just coming in and they hadn't received a call, even though the front line staff acknowledged getting a call from Overlake. My very sick 3 year old was up until 4 am while 12 different people looked at charts and the hospital helped themselves to some fees from my health insurance. I feel stupid and taken advantage of for even making the trip.

reviews.author: Sarah A
reviews.text: This place is AMAZING! All of the doctor were very nice & helpful. We had to stay for 3 days. Nice playroom for the kids. If they can't leave their room, you can bring borad games & other things back to their rooms. Whenever they had a group discussion, they would include me. Thank you Children's Hospital for everything.

reviews.author: Blanca Guerrero
reviews.text: Me gusta

reviews.author: Enrique Rodriguez
reviews.text: I went there to pick up a kid to bring somewhere else and the staff was not only polite and willing but very helpful in giving me precise directions and help on how to get to the room. Facility was very clean; and very warm for adults and children. I hope no one has to bring their child here for being sick; but if your child does get sick; this is the perfect place to make sure your child gets well taken care of. Highly recommend.

reviews.author: bridget barlow
reviews.text: I HAD BEEN ADMITTED TO THE HOSPITAL AFTER SUFFERING A STROKE AT  THE AGE OF 7. LITTLE KNOWN THAT IT WAS THE RESULT OF TYPE 2 JUVENILE DIABETES.  I AM CELEBRATING MY 52 BIRTHDAY TODAY.I WANTED TO REACH OUT AND THANK CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL FOR MAKING THAT A POSSIBILITY.THANK YOUBRIDGET BARLOW

reviews.author: Renee McDougall
reviews.text: Obviously, I hope you never have a need to go here. But, things happen. And if you need your child to be seen by the best, then come here. The doctors and nurses have passion and truly want to help. The staff stopped at nothing to get my daughter the care she needed, even though that meant the doctors and nurses had to learn about her condition and network with doctors and specialists around the world to find answers. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Cul Le
reviews.text: Excellent care

reviews.author: Desirae Fenton
reviews.text: Nice place. Very nice doctors and nurses. They all treat you nice when you are their. I have gone here ever since I was a baby. The place is still the same but more updated and they are adding on. They have one new building and building another one. When you have to go to the doctor on your birthday they give you a little present for your birthday. The play room in the main building is amazing for kids of all ages. You can even go outside and play. They have a swimming pool too.

reviews.author: Kim Plank
reviews.text: My son injured his knee while playing in a baseball tournament.  Seattle Children’s Hospital was near the field and it had the best wait time.  I was unaware that there was a $100 hospital fee until I received my bill (we have excellent insurance).  If that fee had been transparent when we checked in I would have walked out and driven to another urgent care facility in the area.  I called Seattle Children’s hospital to dispute the charge. reviews.author: Lizzie Alfree
reviews.text: My son woke in the middle of the night with a bad asthma attack. I used the inhaler and spacer we had from his last asthma attack he had a year ago. He was still having retractions and a bit of stridor so we drove to the ER. I entered, looked around and then a nurse summoned us over to the desk. Security never once looked up. He assessed my son and found him to have a slight wheeze, took our name and has us sit. We were called to the triage room where the nurse also found him to have a slight expiratory wheeze as well as a very low fever. We then sat in the waiting area until someone called us back to a room. We sat back in the ER room without anyone giving us a call light, telling us how to work the TV/call light, who our nurse would be, or coming in to check on us. I walked out of the room to ask for a blanket and then where the bathroom was. Eventually the resident/student came in and apologized for the wait. She assessed my son. I explained his having had croup at change of seasons back in PA, one asthma attack here last fall resulting in an hour long neb and then this episode. She left and then we had the ER doc come in who basically didn't take a breath as she spoke to me about my son and barely listened to his chest. She left. Initially she wasn't going to give him anything. Not that I am one to dose my kid up but I didn't want his croup to cause any more issues such as the one that brought us in. At some point a tech did come in and do vital signs. We had one set taken during our 4 hour stay within the room. I honestly thought bare minimum was every 2 hours but if I recall correctly it's hourly.  I don't recall her giving us her name, but saw her sauntering about with the other one I had asked and received the blanket from. Eventually our/the nurse finally came in and brought in a syringe with her telling us he was going to get a steroid. I asked if he could have something to drink in order to wash it down and then she said, "It's in cherry syrup." I said I know but when I worked as a nurse (5 years ago before quitting to be a SAHM with my last stint being in the ER for 7)  and gave out meds of any kind I always asked a child if they wanted juice or water to wash the med down. She left, came back and gave him the med. No discharge instructions were given. I had to ask for a note as I wasn't sure if my son would need one for school to be excused for his absence. This ER needs a fast track and lacked some basic nursing care. Looks like they get stellar reviews although I noticed there is a seemingly automated response to reviews and they don't always coincide with the review.  Not sure if this was a fluke or if this is routine and people don't know any better? A call light should be given to family/patient, usage reviewed, checks by techs/aides, if nurses are busy and a blanket offered/given by the person walking us back. These small measures go a long way. I can see why the hospital I worked in was so beloved. We did those things. I have to say we had much better care last year at the Swedish ER. Then they had the nerve to call wanting a automated review. Hopefully we don't need to but if we do, we will go to Swedish.

reviews.author: Boomer Golden
reviews.text: Children’s is a mixed bag. Great care in Bellevue and for most medical stuff in Seattle. Psychiatric and behavioral care is very weak and disappointing, especially compared to care elsewhere at Children’s and in other high quality hospitals out of the area. Our family has had two terrible inpatient experiences here in about 90 days. The staff is inexperienced and low paid, with lots of self disclosed turnover and unhappiness. They seem poorly equipped to do difficult but important jobs. Admins blow smoke and excuses and meaningless apologies and promises to do better at parents who stick around to see what is happening and attend meetings if staff shows up as promised.  They do not communicate with each other or parents or document key things so it is hard to see how psychiatrists and therapists have any info needed to make decisions. A lot falls through the cracks. They throw drugs at the kid and throw her out without any real aftercare lined up. Expect no help even that which was promised in writing after didcharge. And, no, Children’s has no available outpatient slots by and large. Children’s needs to beef up this area to stay top notch especially given lack of quality alternativesHighly recommend for other areasER is very hit or miss. Seems more dependent on who is working than demand

reviews.author: Leea deR
reviews.text: 16 yr old  daughter had a very serious case of H-pylori that her local gastro sent to SCH for post treatment healing help . After 9 months of procrastination and appt's where the Dr never showed , SCH finally said we need to get another opinion. They were convinced it was all in our heads. Child looked like death and was giving up. Local gastro was disgusted as were we . They let minors refuse treatment which is going to make things worse  and it did .  It was really never made  clear to us who we were seeing , I thought we were seeing a gastro team and it turns out they were psychologists ..jeez my god .. Even their ER Dr there was appalled at her lack of treatment when we had to take her back one day after her sudden check out . We finally just took her home and I researched enough on google to help get her healed up the rest of the way and it was extremely tough . She is fair a year later , still HP neg but not the same . SCH had me cancel a very important scope scheduled locally  because they were going to do one , after 3 months I rescheduled  again locally on my own and like we thought , she had gastritis and esophagitis from the H pylori treatment  Her stomach and esophagus were shredded from the treatment and it was not in our heads after all . Simply having a tough time healing . She couldn't eat or drink well at all and was in a tremendous amount of pain and we are insulted they thought all of us were crazy and I didn't appreciate her being shoved off on a herd of psychiatrists  . No rx meds for home or pain management or finding out the CURRENT extent of the gastritis , they just knew it was gone w/o looking . IF you advocate for your child , all of you will be checking out shortly . Just sit and be silent if it is bad enough that you know your child  needs to be there  .Upon check out they cancelled all of our follow up appts they'd made the day before at the team meeting with my husband. I used to love this hospital .  Now I'll never go there again  . Been a mom for 36 years and it is hard to do,  but they managed to shock and disillusion me .This was complicated & messy and you abandoned her.

reviews.author: Chris Toth
reviews.text: It was horrible! Our son had high TSH and normal T4 at birth (thyroid levels were off). Our pediatrician wanted us to see an expert, but also said there was a chance our son could grow out of it at 6-9 months old. We chose to go to Seattle children's hospital due to a few people giving us good reviews. What a mistake! The nurses couldn't figure out how to take blood from an infant. 45 minutes of screaming and 7 tries total from 3 different nurses, and they finally called in an anesthesiologist. He found a vein first try and my son wasn't screaming. Probably helped that he wasn't wiggling the needle around under the skin trying to find a vein. We then went to take some pictures of my son's thyroid. That part was ok. Then onto Dr. Dichek... She wanted to Send us home immediately with hormone replacement (T4) drugs and a prescription for it. All the while his T4 had been normal in every test he had taken up to this point, and the blood taken 30 minutes beforehand wasn't even tested yet! How can a doctor prescribe anything without waiting for their own blood test results to come back? My wife and I decided to leave without the hormones, and thoughts of a second opinion growing. Two days later we get a call from Dr. Dichek informing us that they did not have enough blood to complete the necessary testing, but she wrote us the T4 prescription anyway. That is when we decided that we had to get a second opinion. We found an endocrinologist that is an expert. In the appointment, we were told that as long as our son's T4 was normal then he would be just fine. He also said that some people just have a higher than normal TSH. Then the blood test came back from our new specialist,  and all results are normal. We were also told that if our son had started the T4 medication, then it would have killed his thyroid completely. Glad we decided on a second opinion! How many families just followed these doctors advice and killed their childrens normal thyroid? Now we are stuck with a bill almost totaling to just below $1500 from Seattle Children's Hospital. Thanks for the bad memories!

reviews.text: We recently moved to this area of Seattle. Our previous doctor has referred us to this hospital for speech therapy. We filed another form and sent to them. After that, we waited 2 weeks. We contacted them multiple times, but their phone usually does not respond. Once they responded, they told us to wait more.Finally, representative from hospital speech therapy contacted us to tell... that we just lost our time!!! They have no any therapy here. They can do "evaluation" only. But for some reason she told there is no sense for us to do evaluation. The representative was very busy and told that she has no time to answer our questions. For questions, she referred us to another phone number. That other phone number did no respond, and auto-response said that specialist comes here just couple times a week.This mockery was after we waited a lot of time and spent few HOURS searching information they requested!I think this hospital should close speech therapy department. Because there is no any speech therapy here. And employees there are just spending taxpayers money doing almost nothing!I do not recommend this place to anyone.
